entries.label: Annotation
entries.comment: An annotation is an assertion made in relation to one or more objects.

entries.label: Assertion
entries.comment: An assertion is a statement declared to be true.

entries.label: UcoObject
entries.comment: A UCO object is a representation of a fundamental concept either directly inherent to the cyber domain or indirectly related to the cyber domain and necessary for contextually characterizing cyber domain concepts and relationships. Within the Unified Cyber Ontology (UCO) structure this is the base class acting as a consistent, unifying and interoperable foundation for all explicit and…

entries.label: AttributedName
entries.comment: An attributed name is a name of an entity issued by some attributed naming authority.

entries.label: Bundle
entries.comment: A bundle is a container for a grouping of UCO content with no presumption of shared context.

entries.label: EnclosingCompilation
entries.comment: An enclosing compilation is a container for a grouping of things.

entries.label: Compilation
entries.comment: A compilation is a grouping of things.

entries.label: ConfidenceFacet
entries.comment: A confidence is a grouping of characteristics unique to an asserted level of certainty in the accuracy of some information.

entries.label: Facet
entries.comment: A facet is a grouping of characteristics singularly unique to a particular inherent aspect of a UCO domain object.

entries.label: ContextualCompilation
entries.comment: A contextual compilation is a grouping of things sharing some context (e.g., a set of network connections observed on a given day, all accounts associated with a given person).

entries.label: ControlledVocabulary
entries.comment: A controlled vocabulary is an explicitly constrained set of string values.

entries.label: Event
entries.comment: An Event is a noteworthy occurrence (something that happens or might happen).

entries.label: ExternalReference
entries.comment: Characteristics of a reference to a resource outside of the UCO.

entries.label: UcoInherentCharacterizationThing
entries.comment: A UCO inherent characterization thing is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular inherent aspect of a UCO domain object.

entries.label: Grouping
entries.comment: A grouping is a compilation of referenced UCO content with a shared context.

entries.label: IdentityAbstraction
entries.comment: An identity abstraction is a grouping of identifying characteristics unique to an individual or organization. This class is an ontological structural abstraction for this concept. Implementations of this concept should utilize the identity:Identity class.

entries.label: Item
entries.comment: An item is a distinct article or unit.

entries.label: MarkingDefinitionAbstraction
entries.comment: A marking definition abstraction is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of a specific data marking conveying restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how marked data can be used and shared. This class is an ontological structural abstraction for this concept. Implementations of this concept should utilize the marking:MarkingDefinition class.

entries.label: ModusOperandi
entries.comment: A modus operandi is a particular method of operation (how a particular entity behaves or the resources they use).

entries.label: Relationship
entries.comment: A relationship is a grouping of characteristics unique to an assertion that one or more objects are related to another object in some way.

entries.label: UcoThing
entries.comment: UcoThing is the top-level class for individuals within UCO.

entries.label: UcoType
entries.comment: UcoType is the top-level class for metaclasses within UCO.  An instance of core:UcoType is also an instance of owl:Class, and is or specializes core:UcoThing.

entries.label: statement
entries.comment: A textual statement of an assertion.

entries.label: namingAuthority
entries.comment: Specifies the naming authority that issued the name of the entity.

entries.label: confidence
entries.comment: An asserted level of certainty in the accuracy of some information.

entries.label: constrainingVocabularyReference
entries.comment: A reference to a specification for an explicitly constrained set of string values. The specification may be unstructured (e.g., web page listing string values) or structured (e.g. RDF/OWL enumeration).

entries.label: value
entries.comment: A string value.

entries.label: constrainingVocabularyName
entries.comment: The name of an explicitly constrained set of string values.

entries.label: endTime
entries.comment: The ending time of a time range.

entries.label: startTime
entries.comment: The initial time of a time range.

entries.label: Event Type
entries.comment: An event type specifies a classification type for the event.

entries.label: referenceURL
entries.comment: A URL for some information defined external to the UCO context.

entries.label: definingContext
entries.comment: A description of the context relevant to the definition of a particular external reference identifier.

entries.label: externalIdentifier
entries.comment: An identifier for some information defined external to the UCO context.

entries.label: context
entries.comment: A description of particular contextual affinity.

entries.label: isDirectional
entries.comment: A specification whether or not a relationship assertion is limited to the context FROM a source object(s) TO a target object.

entries.label: kindOfRelationship
entries.comment: A characterization of the nature of a relationship between objects.

entries.label: objectCreatedTime
entries.comment: The time at which a characterization of a concept is created. This time pertains to the time of creating the record object, and is not an intrinsic characteristic of the concept.

entries.label: modifiedTime
entries.comment: Specifies the time that this particular version of the object was modified. The object creator can use the time it deems most appropriate as the time this version of the object was modified. The value of the modified property for a given object version MUST be later than or equal to the value of the created property. Object creators MUST update the modified property when creating a new version of…

entries.label: name
entries.comment: The name of a particular concept characterization.

entries.label: specVersion
entries.comment: The version of UCO ontology or subontology specification used to characterize a concept.

entries.label: description
entries.comment: A description of a particular concept characterization.

entries.label: tag
entries.comment: A generic tag/label.

entries.label: informalType
entries.comment: Informal Type serves as a parent property for string-valued properties meant to describe a type without implementing a class design.  This property hierarchy supports a balancing point between semantic specificity and operational agility.  The known benefits of describing types rather than implementing them include swift extensibility of some existing, or possibly non-existing, subclass hierarchy…

entries.label: object
entries.comment: Specifies one or more UcoObjects.

entries.label: Event Context
entries.comment: An event context describes the association of actions and objects relating to an event.

entries.label: Event Attribute
entries.comment: An event attribute specifies an ad-hoc attribute/value for an event.

entries.label: target
entries.comment: The terminating node of a specified relationship.

entries.label: source
entries.comment: The originating node of a specified relationship.

entries.label: External Reference
entries.comment: Specifies a reference to a resource outside of the UCO.

entries.label: hasFacet
entries.comment: Further sets of properties characterizing a concept based on the particular context of the class and of the particular instance of the concept being characterized.

entries.label: createdBy
entries.comment: The identity that created a characterization of a concept.

entries.label: objectMarking
entries.comment: Marking definitions to be applied to a particular concept characterization in its entirety.

entries.label: objectStatus
entries.comment: The current state of formality and acceptance for a UCO object.

entries.label: API
entries.comment: An API (application programming interface) is a computing interface that defines interactions between multiple software or mixed hardware-software intermediaries. It defines the kinds of calls or requests that can be made, how to make them, the data formats that should be used, the conventions to follow, etc. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API]

entries.label: ObservableObject
entries.comment: An observable object is a grouping of characteristics unique to a distinct article or unit within the digital domain.

entries.label: ARPCache
entries.comment: An ARP cache is a collection of Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) entries (mostly dynamic) that are created when an IP address is resolved to a MAC address (so the computer can effectively communicate with the IP address). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARP_cache]

entries.label: ARPCacheEntry
entries.comment: An ARP cache entry is a single Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) response record that is created when an IP address is resolved to a MAC address (so the computer can effectively communicate with the IP address). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARP_cache]

entries.label: Account
entries.comment: An account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service.

entries.label: AccountAuthenticationFacet
entries.comment: An account authentication facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the mechanism of accessing an account.

entries.label: AccountFacet
entries.comment: An account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service.

entries.label: Adaptor
entries.comment: An adaptor is a device that physically converts the pin outputs but does not alter the underlying protocol (e.g. uSD to SD, CF to ATA, etc.)

entries.label: Device
entries.comment: A device is a piece of equipment or a mechanism designed to serve a special purpose or perform a special function. [based on https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/device]

entries.label: Address
entries.comment: An address is an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of information.

entries.label: AlternateDataStream
entries.comment: An alternate data stream is data content stored within an NTFS file that is independent of the standard content stream of the file and is hidden from access by default NTFS file viewing mechanisms.

entries.label: FileSystemObject
entries.comment: A file system object is an informational object represented and managed within a file system.

entries.label: AlternateDataStreamFacet
entries.comment: An alternate data stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to data content stored within an NTFS file that is independent of the standard content stream of the file and is hidden from access by default NTFS file viewing mechanisms.

entries.label: AndroidDevice
entries.comment: An Android device is a device running the Android operating system. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system)]

entries.label: AndroidDeviceFacet
entries.comment: An Android device facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an Android device. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system)]

entries.label: AndroidPhone
entries.comment: An android phone is a smart phone that applies the Android mobile operating system.

entries.label: SmartPhone
entries.comment: A smartphone is a portable device that combines mobile telephone and computing functions into one unit.  Examples include iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, Huawei, Blackberry. (Inferred by model and OperatingSystemFacet)

entries.label: AntennaFacet
entries.comment: An antenna alignment facet contains the metadata surrounding the cell tower's antenna position.

entries.label: AppleDevice
entries.comment: An apple device is a smart device that applies either the MacOS or iOS operating system.

entries.label: Appliance
entries.comment: An appliance is a purpose-built computer with software or firmware that is designed to provide a specific computing capability or resource. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_appliance]

entries.label: Application
entries.comment: An application is a particular software program designed for end users.

entries.label: ApplicationAccount
entries.comment: An application account is an account within a particular software program designed for end users.

entries.label: DigitalAccount
entries.comment: A digital account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service within the digital domain.

entries.label: ApplicationAccountFacet
entries.comment: An application account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an account within a particular software program designed for end users.

entries.label: ApplicationFacet
entries.comment: An application facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular software program designed for end users.

entries.label: ApplicationVersion
entries.comment: An application version is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular software program version.

entries.label: ArchiveFile
entries.comment: An archive file is a file that is composed of one or more computer files along with metadata.

entries.label: File
entries.comment: A file is a computer resource for recording data discretely on a computer storage device.

entries.label: ArchiveFileFacet
entries.comment: An archive file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a file that is composed of one or more computer files along with metadata.

entries.label: Audio
entries.comment: Audio is a digital representation of sound.

entries.label: AudioFacet
entries.comment: An audio facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a digital representation of sound.

entries.label: AutonomousSystem
entries.comment: An autonomous system is a collection of connected Internet Protocol (IP) routing prefixes under the control of one or more network operators on behalf of a single administrative entity or domain that presents a common, clearly defined routing policy to the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_system_(Internet)]

entries.label: AutonomousSystemFacet
entries.comment: An autonomous system facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a collection of connected Internet Protocol (IP) routing prefixes under the control of one or more network operators on behalf of a single administrative entity or domain that presents a common, clearly defined routing policy to the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_system_(Internet)]

entries.label: BlackberryPhone
entries.comment: A blackberry phone is a smart phone that applies the Blackberry OS mobile operating system. (Blackberry 10 re-introduces Blackberry OS, prior to that the OS was Android.)

entries.label: BlockDeviceNode
entries.comment: A block device node is a UNIX filesystem special file that serves as a conduit to communicate with devices, providing buffered randomly accesible input and output. Block device nodes are used to apply access rights to the devices and to direct operations on the files to the appropriate device drivers. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_file_types]

entries.label: BluetoothAddress
entries.comment: A Bluetooth address is a Bluetooth standard conformant identifier assigned to a Bluetooth device to enable routing and management of Bluetooth standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: MACAddress
entries.comment: A MAC address is a media access control standards conformant identifier assigned to a network interface to enable routing and management of communications at the data link layer of a network segment.

entries.label: BluetoothAddressFacet
entries.comment: A Bluetooth address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Bluetooth standard conformant identifier assigned to a Bluetooth device to enable routing and management of Bluetooth standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: MACAddressFacet
entries.comment: A MAC address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a media access control standards conformant identifier assigned to a network interface to enable routing and management of communications at the data link layer of a network segment.

entries.label: BotConfiguration
entries.comment: A bot configuration is a set of contextual settings for a software application that runs automated tasks (scripts) over the Internet at a much higher rate than would be possible for a human alone.

entries.label: BrowserBookmark
entries.comment: A browser bookmark is a saved shortcut that directs a WWW (World Wide Web) browser software program to a particular WWW accessible resource. [based on https://techterms.com/definition/bookmark]

entries.label: BrowserBookmarkFacet
entries.comment: A browser bookmark facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a saved shortcut that directs a WWW (World Wide Web) browser software program to a particular WWW accessible resource. [based on https://techterms.com/definition/bookmark]

entries.label: BrowserCookie
entries.comment: A browser cookie is a piece of of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the user's web browser while the user is browsing. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_cookie]

entries.label: BrowserCookieFacet
entries.comment: A browser cookie facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a piece of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the user's web browser while the user is browsing. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_cookie]

entries.label: Calendar
entries.comment: A calendar is a collection of appointments, meetings, and events.

entries.label: CalendarEntry
entries.comment: A calendar entry is an appointment, meeting or event within a collection of appointments, meetings and events.

entries.label: CalendarEntryFacet
entries.comment: A calendar entry facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an appointment, meeting, or event within a collection of appointments, meetings, and events.

entries.label: CalendarFacet
entries.comment: A calendar facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a collection of appointments, meetings, and events.

entries.label: Call
entries.comment: A call is a connection as part of a realtime cyber communication between one or more parties.

entries.label: CallFacet
entries.comment: A call facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a connection as part of a realtime cyber communication between one or more parties.

entries.label: CapturedTelecommunicationsInformationFacet
entries.comment: A captured telecommunications information facet represents certain information within captured or intercepted telecommunications data.

entries.label: CellSiteFacet
entries.comment: A cell site facet contains the metadata surrounding the cell site.

entries.label: CharacterDeviceNode
entries.comment: A character device node is a UNIX filesystem special file that serves as a conduit to communicate with devices, providing only a serial stream of input or accepting a serial stream of output. Character device nodes are used to apply access rights to the devices and to direct operations on the files to the appropriate device drivers. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_file_types]

entries.label: Code
entries.comment: Code is a direct representation (source, byte or binary) of a collection of computer instructions that form software which tell a computer how to work. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software]

entries.label: CompressedStreamFacet
entries.comment: A compressed stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the application of a size-reduction process to a body of data content.

entries.label: Computer
entries.comment: A computer is an electronic device for storing and processing data, typically in binary, according to instructions given to it in a variable program. [based on 'Computer.' Oxford English Dictionary, Oxford University Press, 2022.]

entries.label: ComputerSpecification
entries.comment: A computer specification is the hardware and software of a programmable electronic device that can store, retrieve, and process data. {based on merriam-webster.com/dictionary/computer]

entries.label: ComputerSpecificationFacet
entries.comment: A computer specificaiton facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the hardware and software of a programmable electronic device that can store, retrieve, and process data. [based on merriam-webster.com/dictionary/computer]

entries.label: ConfiguredSoftware
entries.comment: A ConfiguredSoftware is a Software that is known to be configured to run in a more specified manner than some unconfigured or less-configured Software.

entries.label: Software
entries.comment: Software is a definitely scoped instance of a collection of data or computer instructions that tell the computer how to work. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software]

entries.label: Contact
entries.comment: A contact is a set of identification and communication related details for a single entity.

entries.label: ContactAddress
entries.comment: A contact address is a grouping of characteristics unique to a geolocation address of a contact entity.

entries.label: ContactListAffiliation
entries.comment: A contact affiliation is a grouping of characteristics unique to details of an organizational affiliation for a single contact entity.

entries.label: ContactEmail
entries.comment: A contact email is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by email.

entries.label: ContactMessaging
entries.comment: A contact messaging is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by digital messaging.

entries.label: ContactPhone
entries.comment: A contact phone is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by telephone.

entries.label: ContactProfile
entries.comment: A contact profile is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by online service.

entries.label: ContactURL
entries.comment: A contact URL is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by Uniform Resource Locator (URL).

entries.label: ContactFacet
entries.comment: A contact facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a set of identification and communication related details for a single entity.

entries.label: ContactSIP
entries.comment: A contact SIP is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by Session Initiation Protocol (SIP).

entries.label: ContactList
entries.comment: A contact list is a set of multiple individual contacts such as that found in a digital address book.

entries.label: ContactListFacet
entries.comment: A contact list facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a set of multiple individual contacts such as that found in a digital address book.

entries.label: ContentData
entries.comment: Content data is a block of digital data.

entries.label: ContentDataFacet
entries.comment: A content data facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a block of digital data.

entries.label: CookieHistory
entries.comment: A cookie history is the stored web cookie history for a particular web browser.

entries.label: Credential
entries.comment: A credential is a single specific login and password combination for authorization of access to a digital account or system.

entries.label: CredentialDump
entries.comment: A credential dump is a collection (typically forcibly extracted from a system) of specific login and password combinations for authorization of access to a digital account or system.

entries.label: DNSCache
entries.comment: An DNS cache is a temporary locally stored collection of previous Domain Name System (DNS) query results (created when an domain name is resolved to a IP address) for a particular computer.

entries.label: DNSRecord
entries.comment: A DNS record is a single Domain Name System (DNS) artifact specifying information of a particular type (routing, authority, responsibility, security, etc.) for a specific Internet domain name.

entries.label: DataRangeFacet
entries.comment: A data range facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular contiguous scope within a block of digital data.

entries.label: DefinedEffectFacet
entries.comment: A defined effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effect of an observable action in relation to one or more observable objects.

entries.label: DeviceFacet
entries.comment: A device facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a piece of equipment or a mechanism designed to serve a special purpose or perform a special function. [based on https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/device]

entries.label: DigitalAccountFacet
entries.comment: A digital account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service within the digital domain.

entries.label: DigitalAddress
entries.comment: A digital address is an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of digital communication.

entries.label: DigitalAddressFacet
entries.comment: A digital address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of digital communication.

entries.label: DigitalCamera
entries.comment: A digital camera is a camera that captures photographs in digital memory as opposed to capturing images on photographic film.

entries.label: DigitalSignatureInfo
entries.comment: A digital signature info is a value calculated via a mathematical scheme for demonstrating the authenticity of an electronic message or document.

entries.label: DigitalSignatureInfoFacet
entries.comment: A digital signature info facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a value calculated via a mathematical scheme for demonstrating the authenticity of an electronic message or document.

entries.label: Directory
entries.comment: A directory is a file system cataloging structure which contains references to other computer files, and possibly other directories. On many computers, directories are known as folders, or drawers, analogous to a workbench or the traditional office filing cabinet. In UNIX a directory is implemented as a special file. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directory_(computing)]

entries.label: Disk
entries.comment: A disk is a storage mechanism where data is recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks.

entries.label: StorageMedium
entries.comment: A storage medium is any digital storage device that applies electromagnetic or optical surfaces, or depends solely on electronic circuits as solid state storage, for storing digital data. Examples include HDD (PATA), SATA, SSD, Optical, Memory_Card, Tape, etc

entries.label: DiskFacet
entries.comment: A disk facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a storage mechanism where data is recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks.

entries.label: DiskPartition
entries.comment: A disk partition is a particular managed region on a storage mechanism where data is recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disk_storage]

entries.label: DiskPartitionFacet
entries.comment: A disk partition facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular managed region on a storage mechanism.

entries.label: DomainName
entries.comment: A domain name is an identification string that defines a realm of administrative autonomy, authority or control within the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name]

entries.label: DomainNameFacet
entries.comment: A domain name facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an identification string that defines a realm of administrative autonomy, authority or control within the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name]

entries.label: Drone
entries.comment: A drone, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), is an aircraft without a human pilot, crew, or passengers that typically involve a ground-based controller and a system for communications with the UAV.

entries.label: MobileDevice
entries.comment: A mobile device is a portable computing device. [based on https://www.lexico.com.definition/mobile_device]

entries.label: EXIFFacet
entries.comment: An EXIF (exchangeable image file format) facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the formats for images, sound, and ancillary tags used by digital cameras (including smartphones), scanners and other systems handling image and sound files recorded by digital cameras conformant to JEIDA/JEITA/CIPA specifications. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exif]

entries.label: EmailAccount
entries.comment: An email account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of electronic mail (email) capabilities or services.

entries.label: EmailAccountFacet
entries.comment: An email account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of electronic mail (email) capabilities or services.

entries.label: EmailAddress
entries.comment: An email address is an identifier for an electronic mailbox to which electronic mail messages (conformant to the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)) are sent from and delivered to.

entries.label: EmailAddressFacet
entries.comment: An email address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an identifier for an electronic mailbox to which electronic mail messages (conformant to the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)) are sent from and delivered to.

entries.label: EmailMessage
entries.comment: An email message is a message that is an instance of an electronic mail correspondence conformant to the internet message format described in RFC 5322 and related RFCs.

entries.label: Message
entries.comment: A message is a discrete unit of electronic communication intended by the source for consumption by some recipient or group of recipients. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Message]

entries.label: EmailMessageFacet
entries.comment: An email message facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a message that is an instance of an electronic mail correspondence conformant to the internet message format described in RFC 5322 and related RFCs.

entries.label: MimePartType
entries.comment: A mime part type is a grouping of characteristics unique to a component of a multi-part email body.

entries.label: EmbeddedDevice
entries.comment: An embedded device is a highly specialized microprocessor device meant for one or very few specific purposes and is usually embedded or included within another object or as part of a larger system. Examples include answer machine, door access logger, card scanner, etc.

entries.label: EncodedStreamFacet
entries.comment: An encoded stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the conversion of a body of data content from one form to another form.

entries.label: EncryptedStreamFacet
entries.comment: An encrypted stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the conversion of a body of data content from one form to another obfuscated form in such a way that reversing the conversion to obtain the original data form can only be accomplished through possession and use of a specific key.

entries.label: EnvironmentVariable
entries.comment: An environment variable is a grouping of characteristics unique to a dynamic-named value that can affect the way running processes will behave on a computer. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_variable]

entries.label: EventLog
entries.comment: An event log is a collection of event records.

entries.label: EventRecord
entries.comment: An event record is something that happens in a digital context (e.g., operating system events).

entries.label: EventRecordFacet
entries.comment: An event record facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to something that happens in a digital context (e.g., operating system events).

entries.label: ObservableAction
entries.comment: An observable action is a grouping of characteristics unique to something that may be done or performed within the digital domain.

entries.label: ExtInodeFacet
entries.comment: An extInode facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a file system object (file, directory, etc.) conformant to the extended file system (EXT or related derivations) specification.

entries.label: ExtractedString
entries.comment: An extracted string is a grouping of characteristics unique to a series of characters pulled from an observable object.

entries.label: ExtractedStringsFacet
entries.comment: An extracted strings facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to one or more sequences of characters pulled from an observable object.

entries.label: URL
entries.comment: A URL is a uniform resource locator (URL) acting as a resolvable address to a particular WWW (World Wide Web) accessible resource.

entries.label: FileFacet
entries.comment: A file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the storage of a file (computer resource for recording data discretely in a computer storage device) on a file system (process that manages how and where data on a storage device is stored, accessed and managed). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/Computer_file and https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5510/file-system]

entries.label: FilePermissionsFacet
entries.comment: A file permissions facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the access rights (e.g., view, change, navigate, execute) of a file on a file system.

entries.label: FileSystem
entries.comment: A file system is the process that manages how and where data on a storage medium is stored, accessed and managed. [based on https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5510/file-system]

entries.label: FileSystemFacet
entries.comment: A file system facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the process that manages how and where data on a storage medium is stored, accessed and managed. [based on https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5510/file-system]

entries.label: ForumPost
entries.comment: A forum post is message submitted by a user account to an online forum where the message content (and typically metadata including who posted it and when) is viewable by any party with viewing permissions on the forum.

entries.label: ForumPrivateMessage
entries.comment: A forum private message (aka PM or DM (direct message)) is a one-to-one message from one specific user account to another specific user account on an online form where transmission is managed by the online forum platform and the message is only viewable by the parties directly involved.

entries.label: FragmentFacet
entries.comment: A fragment facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an individual piece of the content of a file.

entries.label: GUI
entries.comment: A GUI is a graphical user interface that allows users to interact with electronic devices through graphical icons and audio indicators such as primary notation, instead of text-based user interfaces, typed command labels or text navigation. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_user_interface]

entries.label: GamingConsole
entries.comment: A gaming console (video game console or game console) is an electronic system that connects to a display, typically a TV or computer monitor, for the primary purpose of playing video games.

entries.label: GenericObservableObject
entries.comment: A generic observable object is an article or unit within the digital domain.

entries.label: GeoLocationEntry
entries.comment: A geolocation entry is a single application-specific geolocation entry.

entries.label: GeoLocationEntryFacet
entries.comment: A geolocation entry facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a single application-specific geolocation entry.

entries.label: GeoLocationLog
entries.comment: A geolocation log is a record containing geolocation tracks and/or geolocation entries.

entries.label: GeoLocationLogFacet
entries.comment: A geolocation log facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a record containing geolocation tracks and/or geolocation entries.

entries.label: GeoLocationTrack
entries.comment: A geolocation track is a set of contiguous geolocation entries representing a path/track taken.

entries.label: GeoLocationTrackFacet
entries.comment: A geolocation track facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a set of contiguous geolocation entries representing a path/track taken.

entries.label: GlobalFlagType
entries.comment: A global flag type is a grouping of characteristics unique to the Windows systemwide global variable named NtGlobalFlag that enables various internal debugging, tracing, and validation support in the operating system. [based on "Windows Global Flags, Chapter 3: System Mechanisms of Windows Internals by Solomon, Russinovich, and Ionescu]

entries.label: HTTPConnection
entries.comment: An HTTP connection is network connection that is conformant to the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) standard.

entries.label: NetworkConnection
entries.comment: A network connection is a connection (completed or attempted) across a digital network (a group of two or more computer systems linked together). [based on https://www.webopedia.com/TERM/N/network.html]

entries.label: HTTPConnectionFacet
entries.comment: An HTTP connection facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to portions of a network connection that are conformant to the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) standard.

entries.label: Hostname
entries.comment: A hostname is a label that is assigned to a device connected to a computer network and that is used to identify the device in various forms of electronic communication, such as the World Wide Web. A hostname may be a domain name, if it is properly organized into the domain name system. A domain name may be a hostname if it has been assigned to an Internet host and associated with the host's IP…

entries.label: ICMPConnection
entries.comment: An ICMP connection is a network connection that is conformant to the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) standard.

entries.label: ICMPConnectionFacet
entries.comment: An ICMP connection facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to portions of a network connection that are conformant to the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) standard.

entries.label: IComHandlerActionType
entries.comment: An IComHandler action type is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Windows Task-related action that fires a Windows COM handler (smart code in the client address space that can optimize calls between a client and server). [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/comhandleraction]

entries.label: IExecActionType
entries.comment: An IExec action type is a grouping of characteristics unique to an action that executes a command-line operation on a Windows operating system. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/taskschd/nn-taskschd-iexecaction?redirectedfrom=MSDN]

entries.label: IPAddress
entries.comment: An IP address is an Internet Protocol (IP) standards conformant identifier assigned to a device to enable routing and management of IP standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: IPAddressFacet
entries.comment: An IP address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an Internet Protocol (IP) standards conformant identifier assigned to a device to enable routing and management of IP standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: IPNetmask
entries.comment: An IP netmask is a 32-bit 'mask' used to divide an IP address into subnets and specify the network's available hosts.

entries.label: IPhone
entries.comment: An iPhone is a smart phone that applies the iOS mobile operating system.

entries.label: IPv4Address
entries.comment: An IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) address is an IPv4 standards conformant identifier assigned to a device to enable routing and management of IPv4 standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: IPv4AddressFacet
entries.comment: An IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an IPv4 standards conformant identifier assigned to a device to enable routing and management of IPv4 standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: IPv6Address
entries.comment: An IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) address is an IPv6 standards conformant identifier assigned to a device to enable routing and management of IPv6 standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: IPv6AddressFacet
entries.comment: An IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an IPv6 standards conformant identifier assigned to a device to enable routing and management of IPv6 standards conformant communication to or from that device.

entries.label: IShowMessageActionType
entries.comment: An IShow message action type is a grouping of characteristics unique to an action that shows a message box when a task is activate. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/taskschd/nn-taskschd-ishowmessageaction?redirectedfrom=MSDN]

entries.label: Image
entries.comment: An image is a complete copy of a hard disk, memory, or other digital media.

entries.label: ImageFacet
entries.comment: An image facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a complete copy of a hard disk, memory, or other digital media.

entries.label: InstantMessagingAddressFacet
entries.comment: An instant messaging address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of instant messaging digital communication.

entries.label: Junction
entries.comment: A junction is a specific NTFS (New Technology File System) reparse point to redirect a directory access to another directory which can be on the same volume or another volume. A junction is similar to a directory symbolic link but may differ on whether they are processed on the local system or on the remote file server. [based on https://jp-andre.pagesperso-orange.fr/junctions.html]

entries.label: Laptop
entries.comment: A laptop, laptop computer, or notebook computer is a small, portable personal computer with a screen and alphanumeric keyboard. These typically have a clam shell form factor with the screen mounted on the inside of the upper lid and the keyboard on the inside of the lower lid, although 2-in-1 PCs with a detachable keyboard are often marketed as laptops or as having a laptop mode. (Devices…

entries.label: Library
entries.comment: A library is a suite of data and programming code that is used to develop software programs and applications. [based on https://www.techopedia.com/definition/3828/software-library]

entries.label: LibraryFacet
entries.comment: A library facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a suite of data and programming code that is used to develop software programs and applications. [based on https://www.techopedia.com/definition/3828/software-library]

entries.label: Memory
entries.comment: Memory is a particular region of temporary information storage (e.g., RAM (random access memory), ROM (read only memory)) on a digital device.

entries.label: MemoryFacet
entries.comment: A memory facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular region of temporary information storage (e.g., RAM (random access memory), ROM (read only memory)) on a digital device.

entries.label: MessageFacet
entries.comment: A message facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a discrete unit of electronic communication intended by the source for consumption by some recipient or group of recipients. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Message]

entries.label: MessageThread
entries.comment: A message thread is a running commentary of electronic messages pertaining to one topic or question.

entries.label: MessageThreadFacet
entries.comment: A message thread facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a running commentary of electronic messages pertaining to one topic or question.

entries.label: MftRecordFacet
entries.comment: An MFT record facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the details of a single file as managed in an NTFS (new technology filesystem) master file table (which is a collection of information about all files on an NTFS filesystem). [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/devnotes/master-file-table]

entries.label: MobileAccount
entries.comment: A mobile account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service on a portable computing device. [based on https://www.lexico.com/definition/mobile_device]

entries.label: MobileAccountFacet
entries.comment: A mobile account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service on a portable computing device. [based on https://www.lexico.com/definition/mobile_device]

entries.label: MobileDeviceFacet
entries.comment: A mobile device facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a portable computing device. [based on https://www.lexico.com/definition/mobile_device]

entries.label: MobilePhone
entries.comment: A mobile phone is a portable telephone that at least can make and receive calls over a radio frequency link while the user is moving within a telephone service area. This category encompasses all types of mobiles, simple and smart and satellite ones all together.

entries.label: Mutex
entries.comment: A mutex is a mechanism that enforces limits on access to a resource when there are many threads of execution. A mutex is designed to enforce a mutual exclusion concurrency control policy, and with a variety of possible methods there exists multiple unique implementations for different applications. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lock_(computer_science)]

entries.label: MutexFacet
entries.comment: A mutex facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a mechanism that enforces limits on access to a resource when there are many threads of execution. A mutex is designed to enforce a mutual exclusion concurrency control policy, and with a variety of possible methods there exists multiple unique implementations for different applications. [based on…

entries.label: NTFSFile
entries.comment: An NTFS file is a New Technology File System (NTFS) file.

entries.label: NTFSFileFacet
entries.comment: An NTFS file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a file on an NTFS (new technology filesystem) file system.

entries.label: NTFSFilePermissionsFacet
entries.comment: An NTFS file permissions facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the access rights (e.g., view, change, navigate, execute) of a file on an NTFS (new technology filesystem) file system.

entries.label: NamedPipe
entries.comment: A named pipe is a mechanism for FIFO (first-in-first-out) inter-process communication. It is persisted as a filesystem object (that can be deleted like any other file), can be written to or read from by any process and exists beyond the lifespan of any process interacting with it (unlike simple anonymous pipes). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Named_pipe]

entries.label: NetworkAppliance
entries.comment: A network appliance is a purpose-built computer with software or firmware that is designed to provide a specific network management function.

entries.label: NetworkConnectionFacet
entries.comment: A network connection facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a connection (complete or attempted) accross a digital network (a group of two or more computer systems linked together). [based on https://www.webopedia.com/TERM/N/network.html]

entries.label: NetworkFlow
entries.comment: A network flow is a sequence of data transiting one or more digital network (a group or two or more computer systems linked together) connections. [based on https://www.webopedia.com/TERM/N/network.html]

entries.label: NetworkFlowFacet
entries.comment: A network flow facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a sequence of data transiting one or more digital network (a group of two or more computer systems linked together) connections. [based on https://www.webopedia.com/TERM/N/network.html]

entries.label: NetworkInterface
entries.comment: A network interface is a software or hardware interface between two pieces of equipment or protocol layers in a computer network.

entries.label: NetworkInterfaceFacet
entries.comment: A network interface facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a software or hardware interface between two pieces of equipment or protocol layers in a computer network.

entries.label: NetworkProtocol
entries.comment: A network protocol is an established set of structured rules that determine how data is transmitted between different devices in the same network. Essentially, it allows connected devices to communicate with each other, regardless of any differences in their internal processes, structure or design. [based on https://www.comptia.org/content/guides/what-is-a-network-protocol]

entries.label: NetworkRoute
entries.comment: A network route is a specific path (of specific network nodes, connections and protocols) for traffic in a network or between or across multiple networks.

entries.label: NetworkSubnet
entries.comment: A network subnet is a logical subdivision of an IP network. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subnetwork]

entries.label: Note
entries.comment: A note is a brief textual record.

entries.label: NoteFacet
entries.comment: A note facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a brief textual record.

entries.label: Observable
entries.comment: An observable is a characterizable item or action within the digital domain.

entries.label: ObservablePattern
entries.comment: An observable pattern is a grouping of characteristics unique to a logical pattern composed of observable object and observable action properties.

entries.label: ObservableRelationship
entries.comment: An observable relationship is a grouping of characteristics unique to an assertion of an association between two observable objects.

entries.label: Observation
entries.comment: An observation is a temporal perception of an observable.

entries.label: OnlineService
entries.comment: An online service is a particular provision mechanism of information access, distribution or manipulation over the Internet.

entries.label: OnlineServiceFacet
entries.comment: An online service facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular provision mechanism of information access, distribution or manipulation over the Internet.

entries.label: OperatingSystem
entries.comment: An operating system is the software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services for computer programs. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system]

entries.label: OperatingSystemFacet
entries.comment: An operating system facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services for computer programs. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system]

entries.label: PDFFile
entries.comment: A PDF file is a Portable Document Format (PDF) file.

entries.label: PDFFileFacet
entries.comment: A PDF file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a PDF (Portable Document Format) file.

entries.label: PathRelationFacet
entries.comment: A path relation facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the location of one object within another containing object.

entries.label: PaymentCard
entries.comment: A payment card is a physical token that is part of a payment system issued by financial institutions, such as a bank, to a customer that enables its owner (the cardholder) to access the funds in the customer's designated bank accounts, or through a credit account and make payments by electronic funds transfer and access automated teller machines (ATMs). [based on…

entries.label: PhoneAccount
entries.comment: A phone account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of a telephony capability or service.

entries.label: PhoneAccountFacet
entries.comment: A phone account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of a telephony capability or service.

entries.label: Pipe
entries.comment: A pipe is a mechanism for one-way inter-process communication using message passing where data written by one process is buffered by the operating system until it is read by the next process, and this uni-directional channel disappears when the processes are completed. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipeline_(Unix) ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anonymous_pipe]

entries.label: Post
entries.comment: A post is message submitted to an online discussion/publishing site (forum, blog, etc.).

entries.label: Process
entries.comment: A process is an instance of a computer program executed on an operating system.

entries.label: ProcessFacet
entries.comment: A process facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an instance of a computer program executed on an operating system.

entries.label: ProcessThread
entries.comment: A process thread is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler on a computer, which is typically a part of the operating system. It is a component of a process. Multiple threads can exist within one process, executing concurrently and sharing resources such as memory, while different processes do not share these resources. In particular, the…

entries.label: Profile
entries.comment: A profile is an explicit digital representation of identity and characteristics of the owner of a single user account associated with an online service or application. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_profile]

entries.label: ProfileFacet
entries.comment: A profile facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an explicit digital representation of identity and characteristics of the owner of a single user account associated with an online service or application. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_profile]

entries.label: PropertiesEnumeratedEffectFacet
entries.comment: A properties enumerated effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effects of actions upon observable objects where a characteristic of the observable object is enumerated. An example of this would be startup parameters for a process.

entries.label: PropertyReadEffectFacet
entries.comment: A properties read effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effects of actions upon observable objects where a characteristic is read from an observable object. An example of this would be the current running state of a process.

entries.label: ProtocolConverter
entries.comment: A protocol converter is a device that converts from one protocol to another (e.g. SD to USB, SATA to USB, etc.

entries.label: RasterPicture
entries.comment: A raster picture is a raster (or bitmap) image.

entries.label: RasterPictureFacet
entries.comment: A raster picture facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a raster (or bitmap) image.

entries.label: RecoveredObject
entries.comment: An observable object that was the result of a recovery operation.

entries.label: RecoveredObjectFacet
entries.comment: Recoverability status of name, metadata, and content.

entries.label: ReparsePoint
entries.comment: A reparse point is a type of NTFS (New Technology File System) object which is an optional attribute of files and directories meant to define some sort of preprocessing before accessing the said file or directory. For instance reparse points can be used to redirect access to files which have been moved to long term storage so that some application would retrieve them and make them directly…

entries.label: SIMCard
entries.comment: A SIM card is a subscriber identification module card intended to securely store the international mobile subscriber identity (IMSI) number and its related key, which are used to identify and authenticate subscribers on mobile telephony. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIM_card]

entries.label: SIMCardFacet
entries.comment: A SIM card facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a subscriber identification module card intended to securely store the international mobile subscriber identity (IMSI) number and its related key, which are used to identify and authenticate subscribers on mobile telephony devices (such as mobile phones and computers). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIM_card]

entries.label: SIPAddress
entries.comment: A SIP address is an identifier for Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) communication.

entries.label: SIPAddressFacet
entries.comment: A SIP address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) standards conformant identifier assigned to a user to enable routing and management of SIP standards conformant communication to or from that user loosely coupled from any particular devices.

entries.label: SMSMessage

entries.label: SMSMessageFacet
entries.comment: A SMS message facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a message conformant to the short message service (SMS) communication protocol standards.

entries.label: SQLiteBlob
entries.comment: An SQLite blob is a blob (binary large object) of data within an SQLite database. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQLite]

entries.label: SQLiteBlobFacet
entries.comment: An SQLite blob facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a blob (binary large object) of data within an SQLite database. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SQLite]

entries.label: SecurityAppliance
entries.comment: A security appliance is a purpose-built computer with software or firmware that is designed to provide a specific security function to protect computer networks.

entries.label: Semaphore
entries.comment: A semaphore is a variable or abstract data type used to control access to a common resource by multiple processes and avoid critical section problems in a concurrent system such as a multitasking operating system. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semaphore_(programming)]

entries.label: SendControlCodeEffectFacet
entries.comment: A send control code effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effects of actions upon observable objects where a control code, or other control-oriented communication signal, is sent to the observable object. An example of this would be an action sending a control code changing the running state of a process.

entries.label: Server
entries.comment: A server is a server rack-mount based computer, minicomputer, supercomputer, etc.

entries.label: ShopListing
entries.comment: A shop listing is a listing of offered products on an online marketplace/shop.

entries.label: SmartDevice
entries.comment: A smart device is a microprocessor IoT device that is expected to be connected directly to cloud-based networks or via smartphone

entries.label: Snapshot
entries.comment: A snapshot is a file system object representing a snapshot of the contents of a part of a file system at a point in time.

entries.label: Socket
entries.comment: A socket is a special file used for inter-process communication, which enables communication between two processes. In addition to sending data, processes can send file descriptors across a Unix domain socket connection using the sendmsg() and recvmsg() system calls. Unlike named pipes which allow only unidirectional data flow, sockets are fully duplex-capable. [based on…

entries.label: SocketAddress
entries.comment: A socket address (combining and IP address and a port number) is a composite identifier for a network socket endpoint supporting internet protocol communications.

entries.label: SoftwareFacet
entries.comment: A software facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a software program (a definitively scoped instance of a collection of data or computer instructions that tell the computer how to work). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software]

entries.label: StateChangeEffectFacet
entries.comment: A state change effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effects of actions upon observable objects where a state of the observable object is changed.

entries.label: StorageMediumFacet
entries.comment: A storage medium facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a the storage capabilities of a piece of equipment or a mechanism designed to serve a special purpose or perform a special function.

entries.label: SymbolicLink
entries.comment: A symbolic link is a file that contains a reference to another file or directory in the form of an absolute or relative path and that affects pathname resolution. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_link]

entries.label: SymbolicLinkFacet
entries.comment: A symbolic link facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a file that contains a reference to another file or directory in the form of an absolute or relative path and that affects pathname resolution. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbolic_link]

entries.comment: A TCP connection facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to portions of a network connection that are conformant to the Transmission Control Protocl (TCP) standard.

entries.label: TableField
entries.comment: A database table field and its associated value contained within a relational database.

entries.label: TableFieldFacet
entries.comment: A database record facet contains properties associated with a specific table record value from a database.

entries.label: Tablet
entries.comment: A tablet is a mobile computer that is primarily operated by touching the screen. (Devices categorized by their manufacturer as a Tablet)

entries.label: TaskActionType
entries.comment: A task action type is a grouping of characteristics for a scheduled action to be completed.

entries.label: TriggerType
entries.comment: A trigger type is a grouping of characterizes unique to a set of criteria that, when met, starts the execution of a task within a Windows operating system. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/task-triggers]

entries.label: Tweet
entries.comment: A tweet is message submitted by a Twitter user account to the Twitter microblogging platform.

entries.label: TwitterProfileFacet
entries.comment: A twitter profile facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an explicit digital representation of identity and characteristics of the owner of a single Twitter user account. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_profile]

entries.label: UNIXAccount
entries.comment: A UNIX account is an account on a UNIX operating system.

entries.label: UNIXAccountFacet
entries.comment: A UNIX account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an account on a UNIX operating system.

entries.label: UNIXFile
entries.comment: A UNIX file is a file pertaining to the UNIX operating system.

entries.label: UNIXFilePermissionsFacet
entries.comment: A UNIX file permissions facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the access rights (e.g., view, change, navigate, execute) of a file on a UNIX file system.

entries.label: UNIXProcess
entries.comment: A UNIX process is an instance of a computer program executed on a UNIX operating system.

entries.label: UNIXProcessFacet
entries.comment: A UNIX process facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an instance of a computer program executed on a UNIX operating system.

entries.label: UNIXVolumeFacet
entries.comment: A UNIX volume facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a single accessible storage area (volume) with a single UNIX file system. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume_(computing)]

entries.label: URLFacet
entries.comment: A URL facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a uniform resource locator (URL) acting as a resolvable address to a particular WWW (World Wide Web) accessible resource.

entries.label: URLHistory
entries.comment: A URL history characterizes the stored URL history for a particular web browser

entries.label: URL History Entry
entries.comment: A URL history entry is a grouping of characteristics unique to the properties of a single URL history entry for a particular browser.

entries.label: URLHistoryFacet
entries.comment: A URL history facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the stored URL history for a particular web browser

entries.label: URLVisit
entries.comment: A URL visit characterizes the properties of a visit of a URL within a particular browser.

entries.label: URLVisitFacet
entries.comment: A URL visit facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the properties of a visit of a URL within a particular browser.

entries.label: UserAccount
entries.comment: A user account is an account controlling a user's access to a network, system or platform.

entries.label: UserAccountFacet
entries.comment: A user account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an account controlling a user's access to a network, system, or platform.

entries.label: UserSession
entries.comment: A user session is a temporary and interactive information interchange between two or more communicating devices within the managed scope of a single user. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Session_(computer_science)]

entries.label: UserSessionFacet
entries.comment: A user session facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a temporary and interactive information interchange between two or more communicating devices within the managed scope of a single user. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Session_(computer_science)]

entries.label: ValuesEnumeratedEffectFacet
entries.comment: A values enumerated effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effects of actions upon observable objects where a value of the observable object is enumerated. An example of this would be the values of a registry key.

entries.label: Volume
entries.comment: A volume is a single accessible storage area (volume) with a single file system. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume_(computing)]

entries.label: VolumeFacet
entries.comment: A volume facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a single accessible storage area (volume) with a single file system. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume_(computing)]

entries.label: WearableDevice
entries.comment: A wearable device is an electronic device that is designed to be worn on a person's body.

entries.label: WebPage
entries.comment: A web page is a specific collection of information provided by a website and displayed to a user in a web browser. A website typically consists of many web pages linked together in a coherent fashion. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_page]

entries.label: WhoIs

entries.label: WhoIsFacet

entries.label: WhoisRegistrarInfoType
entries.comment: A Whois registrar info type is a grouping of characteristics unique to registrar-related information present in a response record conformant to the WHOIS protocol standard (RFC 3912). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHOIS]

entries.label: WhoIsContactFacet
entries.comment: A Whois contact type is a grouping of characteristics unique to contact-related information present in a response record conformant to the WHOIS protocol standard (RFC 3912). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WHOIS]

entries.label: WifiAddress
entries.comment: A Wi-Fi address is a media access control (MAC) standards-conformant identifier assigned to a device network interface to enable routing and management of IEEE 802.11 standards-conformant communications to and from that device.

entries.label: WifiAddressFacet
entries.comment: A Wi-Fi address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a media access control (MAC) standards conformant identifier assigned to a device network interface to enable routing and management of IEEE 802.11 standards-conformant communications to and from that device.

entries.label: Wiki
entries.comment: A wiki is an online hypertext publication collaboratively edited and managed by its own audience directly using a web browser. A typical wiki contains multiple pages/articles for the subjects or scope of the project and could be either open to the public or limited to use within an organization for maintaining its internal knowledge base. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiki]

entries.label: WikiArticle
entries.comment: A wiki article is one or more pages in a wiki focused on characterizing a particular topic.

entries.label: WindowsAccount
entries.comment: A Windows account is a user account on a Windows operating system.

entries.label: WindowsAccountFacet
entries.comment: A Windows account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a user account on a Windows operating system.

entries.label: WindowsActiveDirectoryAccount
entries.comment: A Windows Active Directory account is an account managed by directory-based identity-related services of a Windows operating system.

entries.label: WindowsActiveDirectoryAccountFacet
entries.comment: A Windows Active Directory account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an account managed by directory-based identity-related services of a Windows operating system.

entries.label: WindowsComputerSpecification
entries.comment: A Windows computer specification is the hardware ans software of a programmable electronic device that can store, retrieve, and process data running a Microsoft Windows operating system. [based on merriam-webster.com/dictionary/computer]

entries.label: WindowsComputerSpecificationFacet
entries.comment: A Windows computer specification facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the hardware and software of a programmable electronic device that can store, retrieve, and process data running a Microsoft Windows operating system. [based on merriam-webster.com/dictionary/computer]
