entries.comment: A role is a usual or customary function based on contextual perspective.

entries.label: MaliciousRole
entries.comment: A malicious role is a role with malevolent intent.

entries.label: NeutralRole
entries.comment: A neutral role is a role with impartial intent.

entries.label: AnalyticTool
entries.comment: An analytic tool is an artifact of hardware and/or software utilized to accomplish a task or purpose of explanation, interpretation or logical reasoning.

entries.label: Tool
entries.comment: A tool is an element of hardware and/or software utilized to carry out a particular function.

entries.label: BuildFacet
entries.comment: A build facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular version of a software.

entries.label: BuildInformationType
entries.comment: A build information type is a grouping of characteristics that describe how a particular version of software was converted from source code to executable code.

entries.label: BuildUtilityType
entries.comment: A build utility type characterizes the tool used to convert from source code to executable code for a particular version of software.

entries.label: CompilerType
entries.comment: A compiler type is a grouping of characteristics unique to a specific program that translates computer code written in one programming language (the source language) into another language (the target language). Typically a program that translates source code from a high-level programming language to a lower-level language (e.g., assembly language, object code, or machine code) to create an…

entries.label: LibraryType
entries.comment: A library type is a grouping of characteristics unique to a collection of resources incorporated into the build of a software.

entries.label: ConfiguredTool
entries.comment: A ConfiguredTool is a Tool that is known to be configured to run in a more specified manner than some unconfigured or less-configured Tool.

entries.label: DefensiveTool
entries.comment: A defensive tool is an artifact of hardware and/or software utilized to accomplish a task or purpose of guarding.

entries.label: MaliciousTool
entries.comment: A malicious tool is an artifact of hardware and/or software utilized to accomplish a malevolent task or purpose.

entries.label: buildInformation
entries.comment: Describes how a particular tool was built.

entries.label: buildConfiguration
entries.comment: How the build utility was configured for a particular build of a particular software.

entries.label: buildUtility
entries.comment: Identifies the utility used to build a software.

entries.label: compilers
entries.comment: The compilers utilized during a particular build of a particular software.

entries.label: libraries
entries.comment: The libraries incorporated into a particular build of a software.

entries.label: creator
entries.comment: The creator organization for a particular tool.

entries.label: compilationDate
entries.comment: The compilation date for the build of a software.

entries.label: buildID
entries.comment: An externally defined unique identifier for a particular build of a software.

entries.label: buildLabel
entries.comment: Relevant label for a particular build of a particular software.

entries.label: buildOutputLog
entries.comment: The output log of the build process for a software.

entries.label: buildProject
entries.comment: The project name of a build of a software.

entries.label: buildScript
entries.comment: The actual build script for a particular build of a particular software.

entries.label: buildVersion
entries.comment: The appropriate version descriptor of a particular build of a particular software.

entries.label: buildUtilityName
entries.comment: The informally defined name of the utility used to build a particular software.

entries.label: cpeid
entries.comment: Specifies the Common Platform Enumeration identifier for the software.

entries.label: swid
entries.comment: Specifies the SWID tag for the software.

entries.label: compilerInformalDescription
entries.comment: An informal description of a compiler.

entries.label: libraryName
entries.comment: The name of the library.

entries.label: libraryVersion
entries.comment: The version of the library.

entries.label: references
entries.comment: References to information describing a particular tool.

entries.label: servicePack
entries.comment: An appropriate service pack descriptor for a particular tool.

entries.label: toolType
entries.comment: The type of tool.

entries.label: version
entries.comment: An appropriate version descriptor of a particular tool.

entries.label: ControlledDictionary
entries.comment: A controlled dictionary is a list of (term/key, value) pairs where each term/key exists no more than once and is constrained to an explicitly defined set of values.

entries.label: ControlledDictionaryEntry
entries.comment: A controlled dictionary entry is a single (term/key, value) pair where the term/key is constrained to an explicitly defined set of values.

entries.label: DictionaryEntry
entries.comment: A dictionary entry is a single (term/key, value) pair.

entries.label: Hash
entries.comment: A hash is a grouping of characteristics unique to the result of applying a mathematical algorithm that maps data of arbitrary size to a bit string (the 'hash') and is a one-way function, that is, a function which is practically infeasible to invert. This is commonly used for integrity checking of data. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_hash_function]

entries.label: ProperDictionary
entries.comment: A proper dictionary is list of (term/key, value) pairs with each term/key existing no more than once.

entries.label: Thread
entries.comment: A semi-ordered array of items, that can be present in multiple copies.  Implementation of a UCO Thread is similar to a Collections Ontology List, except a Thread may fork and merge - that is, one of its members may have two or more direct successors, and two or more direct predecessors.

entries.label: ThreadItem
entries.comment: A ThreadItem is a member of a thread.

entries.label: entry
entries.comment: A dictionary entry.

entries.label: threadNextItem
entries.comment: The link to a next item in a thread.

entries.label: threadSuccessor
entries.comment: A link to a following item in a thread.

entries.label: threadOriginItem
entries.comment: A link to an item of the thread known to have no predecessor.

entries.label: threadPreviousItem
entries.comment: A direct link to a previous item in a thread.

entries.label: threadPredecessor
entries.comment: The link to the preceding item in a thread.

entries.label: threadTerminalItem
entries.comment: A link to an item of the thread known to have no successor.

entries.label: key
entries.comment: A key property of a single dictionary entry.

entries.label: value
entries.comment: A specific property value.

entries.label: hashValue
entries.comment: A cryptographic hash value.

entries.label: hashMethod
entries.comment: A particular cryptographic hashing method (e.g., MD5).

entries.label: repeatsKey
entries.comment: A key found to be repeated in multiple dictionary entries within one dictionary.

entries.label: Victim
entries.comment: A victim is a role played by a person or organization that is/was the target of some malicious action.

entries.label: VictimTargeting
entries.comment: A victim targeting is a grouping of characteristics unique to people or organizations that are the target of some malicious activity.

entries.label: Attorney
entries.comment: Attorney is a role involved in preparing, interpreting, and applying law.

entries.label: Authorization
entries.comment: An authorization is a grouping of characteristics unique to some form of authoritative permission identified for investigative action.

entries.label: Examiner
entries.comment: Examiner is a role involved in providing scientific evaluations of evidence that are used to aid law enforcement investigations and court cases.

entries.label: ExaminerActionLifecycle
entries.comment: An examiner action lifecycle is an action pattern consisting of an ordered set of actions or subordinate action-lifecycles performed by an entity acting in a role involved in providing scientific evaluations of evidence that is used to aid law enforcement investigations and court cases.

entries.label: Investigation
entries.comment: An investigation is a grouping of characteristics unique to an exploration of the facts involved in a cyber-relevant set of suspicious activity.

entries.label: InvestigativeAction
entries.comment: An investigative action is something that may be done or performed within the context of an investigation, typically to examine or analyze evidence or other data.

entries.label: Investigator
entries.comment: Investigator is a role involved in coordinating an investigation.

entries.label: ProvenanceRecord
entries.comment: A provenance record is a grouping of characteristics unique to the provenantial (chronology of the ownership, custody or location) connection between an investigative action and a set of observations (items and/or actions) or interpretations that result from it.

entries.label: Subject
entries.comment: Subject is a role whose conduct is within the scope of an investigation.

entries.label: SubjectActionLifecycle
entries.comment: A subject action lifecycle is an action pattern consisting of an ordered set of multiple actions or subordinate action-lifecycles performed by an entity acting in a role whose conduct may be within the scope of an investigation.

entries.label: VictimActionLifecycle
entries.comment: A victim action lifecycle is an action pattern consisting of an ordered set of multiple actions or subordinate action-lifecycles performed by an entity acting in a role characterized by its potential to be harmed as a result of a crime, accident, or other event or action.

entries.label: authorizationType
entries.comment: A label categorizing a type of authorization (e.g. warrant)

entries.label: authorizationIdentifier
entries.comment: The identifier for a particular authorization (e.g. warrant number)

entries.label: investigationStatus
entries.comment: A label characterizing the status of an investigation (open, closed, etc.).

entries.label: investigationForm
entries.comment: A label categorizing a type of investigation (case, incident, suspicious-activity, etc.)

entries.label: focus
entries.comment: Specifies the topical focus of an investigation.

entries.label: exhibitNumber
entries.comment: The exhibit number specifies an identifier assigned to a set of objects, unique within the scope of an investigation.

entries.label: rootExhibitNumber
entries.comment: The root exhibit number specifies a unique identifier assigned to a set of objects at the start of their treatment as part of an investigation. When found on a provenance record that comes after initial investigative treatment, the root exhibit number is a reference to the initial provenance record.

entries.label: relevantAuthorization
entries.comment: Specifies an authorization relevant to a particular investigation.

entries.label: wasInformedBy
entries.comment: A re-implementation of the wasInformedBy property in W3C PROV-O, where an entity is exchanged by two activities, 'one activity using the entity generated by the other'. [Ref: https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/#wasInformedBy]

entries.label: wasDerivedFrom
entries.comment: A re-implementation of the wasDerivedFrom property in W3C PROV-O.  The definition of this property is 'A derivation is a transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity.' [Ref: https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/#wasDerivedFrom]

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Technique
entries.comment: A digital forensic technique representing how one might achieve an objective by performing an action. Based on the SOLVE-IT knowledge base. This class is a metaclass: its instances are owl:Class entities whose own instances are investigative actions, planned or performed.

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Weakness
entries.comment: A potential problem resulting from using a technique, classified according to ASTM E3016-18 error categories.

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Mitigation
entries.comment: An action that can be performed to prevent a weakness from occurring or to minimize its impact.

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Objective
entries.comment: A goal or objective in a digital forensic investigation that can be achieved through one or more techniques.

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Citation
entries.comment: An academic or professional reference cited by a Technique, Weakness or Mitigation. Each citation carries an identifier (DFCite-NNNN), a plain text form, and where available a BibTeX form.

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Investigative Action
entries.comment: An investigative action, which may be done or performed, as an instance of one or more SOLVE-IT techniques, recording any mitigations applied on that occasion (0..n via appliedMitigation). The technique(s) used are expressed by rdf:type against the technique class(es), not by a separate property.

entries.label: ASTM Error Category
entries.comment: An error category from ASTM E3016-18 used to classify weakness impacts.

entries.label: has reference
entries.comment: Links a Technique, Weakness or Mitigation to a Citation. This was a datatype property carrying the citation identifier as a string; citations became resources in their own right so that the plain text and BibTeX forms have somewhere to live.

entries.label: has potential weakness
entries.comment: Links a Technique to potential weaknesses (error categories from ASTM E3016-18) that may occur when using this technique.

entries.label: has subtechnique
entries.comment: Links a Technique to more specific subtechniques.

entries.label: has potential mitigation
entries.comment: Links a Weakness to mitigations that can potentially prevent or minimize it.

entries.label: links to technique
entries.comment: Links a Mitigation to the Technique(s) it is relevant for or applies to.

entries.label: includes technique
entries.comment: Links an Objective to Techniques that can be used to achieve it.

entries.label: used technique (deprecated)
entries.comment: DEPRECATED. Formerly linked a SolveitInvestigativeAction to the SOLVE-IT Technique definition(s) executed. Superseded by typing the action with the technique class itself, following the uco-action:Technique metaclass pattern.

entries.label: applied mitigation
entries.comment: Links a SolveitInvestigativeAction to Mitigation(s) that were actively applied during the execution to prevent or minimize potential weaknesses (0..n).

entries.label: has CASE input class
entries.comment: A CASE/UCO term that represents an expected input to this technique. Usually a class (e.g., solveit-observable:WriteProtectedDeviceInterface), but a property where the technique consumes a single value rather than an object (e.g., uco-observable:filePath). No rdfs:range is asserted, because no single one is true of both; :TechniqueIOTermShape carries the constraint instead.

entries.label: has CASE output class
entries.comment: A CASE/UCO term that represents an output of this technique. Usually a class (e.g., uco-observable:Image), but a property where the technique produces a single value rather than an object (e.g., case-investigation:exhibitNumber). No rdfs:range is asserted, because no single one is true of both; :TechniqueIOTermShape carries the constraint instead.

entries.label: has weakness class
entries.comment: Associates a weakness with an ASTM E3016-18 error category.

entries.label: technique ID
entries.comment: The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT technique (e.g., T1002).

entries.label: technique name
entries.comment: The name of the technique (e.g., 'Disk imaging').

entries.label: technique description
entries.comment: A detailed description of how the technique is performed.

entries.label: technique details
entries.comment: Additional details about the technique.

entries.label: weakness ID
entries.comment: The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT weakness (e.g., W1004).

entries.label: weakness name
entries.comment: The name describing the weakness.

entries.label: weakness description
entries.comment: A detailed description of the weakness and its potential impacts.

entries.label: mitigation ID
entries.comment: The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT mitigation (e.g., M1001).

entries.label: mitigation name
entries.comment: The name describing the mitigation action.

entries.label: mitigation description
entries.comment: A detailed description of how the mitigation prevents or minimizes a weakness.

entries.label: objective name
entries.comment: The name of the objective.

entries.label: objective ID
entries.comment: The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT objective.

entries.label: objective description
entries.comment: A detailed description of what this objective seeks to achieve.

entries.label: sort order
entries.comment: The position of an objective in investigation order, which is the order the knowledge base presents them in rather than alphabetical order.

entries.label: citation ID
entries.comment: The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT citation (e.g., DFCite-1107).

entries.label: citation plain text
entries.comment: The reference written out as plain text.

entries.label: citation BibTeX
entries.comment: The reference as a BibTeX entry, where one is available.

entries.label: has synonym
entries.comment: Alternative name or synonym for a Technique.

entries.label: has example
entries.comment: Example tool, implementation, or instance for a Technique.

entries.label: INCOMP
entries.comment: Incompleteness — failure to recover live or deleted artefacts (ASTM E3016-18).

entries.label: INAC-EX
entries.comment: Inaccuracy: Existence — presenting artefacts for non-existent items (ASTM E3016-18).

entries.label: INAC-AS
entries.comment: Inaccuracy: Association — e.g. presenting live data as deleted (ASTM E3016-18).

entries.label: INAC-ALT
entries.comment: Inaccuracy: Alteration — modifying the content of digital data (ASTM E3016-18).

entries.label: INAC-COR
entries.comment: Inaccuracy: Corruption — process could corrupt data or fail to detect corrupt data (ASTM E3016-18).

entries.label: MISINT
entries.comment: Misinterpretation — results presented in a way that encourages misinterpretation (ASTM E3016-18).

entries.label: Hypothesis
entries.comment: A statement that is either true or false, the truth of which is uncertain.

entries.label: Hypothesised Event
entries.comment: An event that is hypothesised to have occurred.

entries.label: Hypothesised Web Search
entries.comment: A web search that is hypothesised to have been performed, potentially inferred from browser history fragments, cached results, or suggested search terms. Use uco-observable:keywordSearchTerm for the search query.

entries.label: Hypothesised Communication
entries.comment: A communication that is hypothesised to have occurred between parties, potentially inferred from partial message records, contact patterns, or metadata fragments. Use uco-observable:from and uco-observable:to for the parties involved.

entries.label: Hypothesised Relationship
entries.comment: A relationship between entities that is hypothesised to exist. This covers inferred associations between persons, accounts, devices or locations - drawn from co-occurrence patterns, shared identifiers, or behavioural analysis - and also structural claims such as attributing a recovered database record to the table it belonged to. Being a uco-core:Relationship, the entities are named with…

entries.label: Hypothesised Device
entries.comment: A device that is hypothesised to have been involved, such as a device inferred from artifacts but not yet physically identified or examined.

entries.label: Hypothesised User Account
entries.comment: A user account that is hypothesised to have existed, for example inferred from recovered deleted account records, carved registry artifacts, or references to the account in other artifacts.

entries.label: Hypothesised Record
entries.comment: A database record hypothesised to have existed, typically reconstructed from deallocated or partially overwritten storage such as freeblocks, unallocated page space, or freelist pages. The claim it makes is one of extent: that these bytes constituted one record, beginning and ending where the reconstruction says. That claim can fail - a sequence of ordinary integers can decode as a plausible…

entries.label: Hypothesised Table Attribution
entries.comment: The claim that a recovered record belonged to a particular table. The record is the uco-core:source and the table the uco-core:target; neither is itself in doubt, only the link between them. Attribution rests on different grounds in different cases - a record recovered from a freeblock sits on a page owned by a known table, whereas one recovered from a freelist page has lost that context and can…

entries.label: Hypothesised Configuration
entries.comment: A configuration proposed from the artefacts it left behind, where the configuration itself was never observed - as distinct from one read directly from a settings file or a live system. Settings are given with uco-configuration:configurationEntry and what was configured with uco-configuration:isConfigurationOf.

entries.label: Hypothesis Set
entries.comment: A collection of competing alternative hypotheses considered together, for example the mutually exclusive explanations proposed for a single observation. Members are linked with solveit-analysis:hasHypothesis.

entries.label: Forensic Tool Tag-Based Report
entries.comment: A report generated by a forensic tool based on tags added during analysis.

entries.label: has hypothesis
entries.comment: Links a HypothesisSet to a member Hypothesis it groups as a competing alternative. Members must be a Hypothesis or a subclass of one, which is enforced by HypothesisSetShape rather than by an rdfs:range. A range would state the requirement without enforcing it: rdfs:range is an entailment rule, so under inference anything placed in a set would thereby be typed a Hypothesis, and putting an…

entries.label: has field
entries.comment: Links a hypothesised record to a decoded field value. It is deliberately not solveit-observable:hasField, whose rdfs:domain is solveit-observable:SQLiteRecord: rdfs:domain is an entailment rule rather than a usage restriction, so reusing that property would infer the hypothesis to be an observed record. The hedge is carried once, by the class, which is why this property needs no 'hypothesised'…

entries.label: hypothesised date time
entries.comment: The date and time at which the hypothesised event is believed to have occurred - either an absolute timestamp (DateTimeStamp) or a time interval (DateTimeRange).

entries.label: has artifact
entries.comment: Links a ForensicToolTagBasedReport to tagged artifacts.

entries.label: has file
entries.comment: Links a ForensicToolTagBasedReport to tagged files.

entries.label: hypothesised rowid
entries.comment: The rowid this record is believed to have had, where recovery preserved it. Freeblock recovery overwrites the cell header, so a rowid is often not available.

entries.label: hypothesised service name
entries.comment: The name of the service or platform hypothesised to have been used (e.g. Google, WhatsApp, iMessage).

entries.label: Bitstream
entries.comment: A sequential, complete bit-for-bit copy of a storage medium (LBA0 to LBAmax). Represents data in transit from a capture process to a storage format.

entries.label: Bitstream Random Accessed
entries.comment: Random access to sector-level data, whether from a live device or a decoded forensic image container. Enables partition parsing, filesystem traversal, and logical operations.

entries.label: Video File
entries.comment: A file whose primary content is video data (e.g. MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV).

entries.label: Audio File
entries.comment: A file whose primary content is audio data (e.g. MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC).

entries.label: Video Frame
entries.comment: A single frame extracted from a video file during forensic analysis.

entries.label: Network Packet Capture
entries.comment: A network packet capture file.

entries.label: Decryption Key
entries.comment: A cryptographic key intended for decryption.

entries.label: Unlock Pattern
entries.comment: A pattern used to unlock a device, i.e. screen lock pattern.

entries.label: File Set
entries.comment: A contextual compilation of files grouped together for some purpose, such as filtering, extraction, or association with an application.

entries.label: Filtered File Set
entries.comment: A subset of files selected from a larger collection by some filtering criteria, such as file type, path, date range, or relevance to an investigation.

entries.label: Redacted File Set
entries.comment: A subset of files reduced by a redaction process to remove sensitive or privileged content before disclosure.

entries.label: Artifact Set
entries.comment: A contextual compilation of forensic artifacts grouped together for some purpose, such as filtering, redaction, or association with an investigation.

entries.label: Redacted Artifact Set
entries.comment: A collection of artifacts reduced by a redaction process to remove sensitive or privileged content before disclosure.

entries.label: HTTP Response Header
entries.comment: An HTTP response header containing multiple header fields from an HTTP server response.

entries.label: Device Interface
entries.comment: A logical interface representing a direct connection to a storage device, such as a USB, SATA.

entries.label: Write Protected Device Interface
entries.comment: A logical interface to a storage device that has been interfaced with in a write-protected manner, either via a hardware write blocker, software write blocking, or a read-only boot environment.

entries.label: Live OS Device Interface
entries.comment: Access to a block device via the operating system on a live, running system. Provides sector-level access to storage without relying on the OS for file system parsing.

entries.label: Read Write Device Interface
entries.comment: A logical interface to a storage device that has been interfaced with in a read-write manner, as yet, without write protection.

entries.label: Hash Verification Result
entries.comment: The result of comparing hash values to verify data integrity, typically comparing a source hash against a computed hash of acquired or copied data.

entries.label: Wordlist
entries.comment: A list of words or terms used as input to techniques such as keyword searching or dictionary-based password attacks. May be a case-type wordlist (standard terms for a category of investigation), a case-specific wordlist (names, addresses, dates etc. specific to the investigation), or a general-purpose dictionary (e.g. for password recovery).

entries.label: Cluster Run
entries.comment: A contiguous run of clusters allocated to a file in a cluster-based file system (e.g., FAT, NTFS, exFAT). Multiple runs indicate file fragmentation.

entries.label: Application Files
entries.comment: A contextual compilation of files associated with a specific application version. Groups the files belonging to a particular application (e.g. WhatsApp v13.2 database files) for forensic examination.

entries.label: Browser App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a web browser application, including browsing history, bookmarks, cookies, saved passwords, session data, and extensions.

entries.label: Browser Cache Data
entries.comment: The locally cached data stored by a web browser to improve performance. This may include cached web pages, images, scripts, and associated metadata. The storage format varies by browser (e.g. Chrome simple cache, Firefox cache2, SQLite indexes).

entries.label: Calendar App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a calendar application, including events, appointments, invitations, recurring schedules, and attendee data (e.g. Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar).

entries.label: Chat App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a messaging or chat application, including message databases, media attachments, contact lists, and encryption key material (e.g. WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram).

entries.label: AI Chat App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with an AI chatbot or assistant application, including conversation histories, prompt logs, cached model responses, and user preference data (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini).

entries.label: Email App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with an email client application, including message stores, mailbox databases, attachments, contact data, and account configuration (e.g. Outlook, Apple Mail, Gmail app).

entries.label: Health App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a health or fitness tracking application, including activity logs, heart rate data, sleep records, workout history, and medical records (e.g. Apple Health, Google Fit, Fitbit).

entries.label: Maps App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a mapping application, including search history, saved locations, offline map tiles, and location history (e.g. Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze).

entries.label: Navigation App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a turn-by-turn navigation application, including route history, recent destinations, favourite locations, and trip logs (e.g. Waze, TomTom, Garmin).

entries.label: Photos App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a photos or gallery management application, including image and video databases, album metadata, facial recognition data, location tags, and editing history (e.g. Apple Photos, Google Photos, Samsung Gallery).

entries.label: Payment App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a mobile payment or digital wallet application, including transaction history, linked accounts, merchant data, and receipts (e.g. Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo).

entries.label: Reminders App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a reminders or to-do list application, including task lists, due dates, recurring reminders, and completion history (e.g. Apple Reminders, Google Tasks, Todoist).

entries.label: Gaming App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a gaming application, including save data, player profiles, in-app purchase records, chat logs, friend lists, and gameplay statistics (e.g. Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, Epic Games, Roblox, mobile games).

entries.label: Social Media App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a social media application, including posts, direct messages, friend/follower lists, media uploads, and notification data (e.g. Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X).

entries.label: Smart Home App Files
entries.comment: Files associated with a smart home or IoT control application, including device registries, automation routines, activity logs, sensor data, camera event histories, and network configuration (e.g. Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Samsung SmartThings).

entries.label: Device Set
entries.comment: A contextual compilation of devices that are associated in some way, such as devices belonging to the same suspect, devices seized from the same location, or devices connected to the same network.

entries.label: Prioritized Device Set
entries.comment: A device set where each device has been triaged and assigned a priority classification. Contains PrioritizedDeviceEntry instances that pair each device with its priority.

entries.label: Prioritized Device Entry
entries.comment: An entry pairing a device with its triage priority classification.

entries.label: Hash Set
entries.comment: A reference set of known file hashes used to match against files under examination, in order to reduce or flag the files examined (e.g. NSRL RDS). Composed of HashSetEntry instances.

entries.label: Hash Set Entry
entries.comment: A single entry within a hash set. At minimum it carries a hash value; further details (e.g. file name, size, product or operating system, classification) may be added as required.

entries.label: Virtualized Device
entries.comment: A device or system that exists as a virtual machine, defined by virtualization configuration and one or more virtual disks rather than running on dedicated physical hardware. A virtualized device may arise in several ways, for example a virtual machine recovered from a suspect's storage, a forensic image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine built as an analysis…

entries.label: Virtualized Computer
entries.comment: A computer (desktop, laptop, or server) that exists as a virtual machine rather than running on physical hardware. The most common form is a server running as a virtual machine in a datacentre or cloud environment, which may itself be the subject of an investigation or host evidence. In a forensic context a virtualized computer may also, for example, be a virtual machine recovered from seized…

entries.label: extracted from video
entries.comment: Links a VideoFrame to the source video file.

entries.label: virtualized from file
entries.comment: Links a virtualized device to the file or files that constitute its virtual machine, such as a configuration file (e.g. .vmx) and one or more virtual disk files (e.g. .vmdk). Multiple files can be linked.

entries.label: unlock pattern sequence
entries.comment: An ordered list of grid positions (integers) representing the unlock pattern sequence. For example, a 3x3 grid uses positions 1-9.

entries.label: has device
entries.comment: A device belonging to this device set.

entries.label: has entry
entries.comment: A prioritized device entry in this set.

entries.label: entry device
entries.comment: The device in this prioritized entry.

entries.label: entry priority
entries.comment: The triage priority classification for this device, using cacontology-forensics:priorityClassification values.

entries.label: source application
entries.comment: The application associated with these files.

entries.label: write protected by
entries.comment: The hardware device or configured software that applies write protection to this interface.

entries.label: has file
entries.comment: A file belonging to this file set.

entries.label: has artifact
entries.comment: An artifact belonging to this artifact set.

entries.label: has cluster run
entries.comment: Links a file to its cluster allocation runs. A contiguous file has one run; a fragmented file has multiple runs.

entries.label: has operating system
entries.comment:
An operating system installed on this device.

Installed rather than running: a powered-off device still has its operating
systems, and that is the state most forensic targets are examined in. More than
one is expected, as a dual-boot machine has two.

Not uco-observable:operatingSystem, which declares no domain and is used on
ApplicationFacet for the system an application runs on.

entries.label: provides access to
entries.comment:
The storage medium that this device interface gives access to.

The interface is a way of reaching the medium, not the medium itself, so the
medium's characteristics (model, serial number, capacity) are stated on the
StorageMedium through its DeviceFacet and StorageMediumFacet, not on the
interface. The same medium can be reached through a write-protected interface
on one occasion and a…

entries.label: contains hash set entry
entries.comment: Links a hash set to one of the entries it contains.

entries.label: contains hash
entries.comment: The hash value carried by a hash set entry. The algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, etc.) is held within the uco-types:Hash instance via its hashMethod and hashValue.

entries.label: frame number
entries.comment: The sequential number of this frame in the video.

entries.label: width
entries.comment: Video frame width in pixels.

entries.label: height
entries.comment: Video frame height in pixels.

entries.label: verification passed
entries.comment: Indicates whether the hash verification was successful (true) or failed (false).

entries.label: run start cluster
entries.comment: The first cluster number in this contiguous run.

entries.label: run cluster count
entries.comment: The number of contiguous clusters in this run.

entries.label: Acquired Data
entries.comment: Data that has been forensically collected from a source device or system. This is the parent class for all types of forensic data acquisition outputs.

entries.label: Forensic Image Container
entries.comment: A forensic image in a container format that encapsulates acquired data, potentially compressed or encrypted, along with embedded metadata such as case information, examiner identity, acquisition timestamps, hash values, compression settings, and encryption status. It may be stored across one or more files referenced via storedIn.

entries.label: Physical Image Container
entries.comment: A forensic image container that encapsulates a bitstream (bit-for-bit) copy of a source medium, such as a full disk image in E01 or AFF4 format.

entries.label: Logical Image Container
entries.comment: A forensic image container that encapsulates a logical collection of files rather than a bitstream copy, such as a logical image in L01 or ZIP format.

entries.label: Raw Image
entries.comment: A raw forensic image containing a bitstream without container metadata. Unlike a ForensicImageContainer (e.g. E01, AFF4), a raw image has no embedded metadata. It may be stored across one or more files (e.g. split .dd segments) referenced via storedIn. Typically accompanied by a RawImageInfoFile containing hashes, case information, and acquisition details.

entries.label: Raw Image Info File
entries.comment: A sidecar file containing metadata for a raw/dd forensic image, including hash values, case information, evidence numbers, examiner details, and acquisition notes. Compensates for the lack of embedded metadata in raw image formats.

entries.label: Acquisition Record File
entries.comment: A file containing records generated during a data acquisition process, such as error logs or acquisition status reports.

entries.label: Live Data Capture
entries.comment: Volatile or transient data captured from a running system at a specific point in time. Includes running processes, memory state, network connections, device interrogation data (e.g., ideviceinfo output), and system properties.

entries.label: File System Extraction
entries.comment: Data obtained through direct access to a file system structure. Represents the files and folders as they existed on the device or storage, applicable to any device type (mobile, desktop, embedded). Live files only.

entries.label: Service-Based Extraction Data
entries.comment: Data obtained by interacting with services provided by a device rather than direct storage access.

entries.label: Device Generated Backup
entries.comment: Data produced by a device's built-in backup mechanism. Content is determined by the device's backup logic and structured in the backup's native format.

entries.label: iOS Device Generated Backup
entries.comment: Data produced by the iOS backup mechanism via iTunes, Finder, or libimobiledevice. Contains a manifest database (Manifest.db), file blobs identified by domain-path hashes, and metadata plists including device information and backup status.

entries.label: Android Device Generated Backup
entries.comment: Data produced by Android's backup mechanism (e.g., adb backup). Potentially contains application data, shared storage, and system settings in the Android backup format (.ab file).

entries.label: AFC Extraction Data
entries.comment: Data obtained via Apple File Conduit (AFC) service from iOS devices.

entries.label: ADB Pull Data
entries.comment: Data obtained via Android Debug Bridge (ADB) pull operations.

entries.label: Apple Unified Log Archive
entries.comment: Data obtained by collecting Apple Unified Logs from a macOS or iOS device.

entries.label: Content Query Data
entries.comment: Data obtained from an Android device by querying content providers via an ADB shell connection (e.g., adb shell content query). Content providers expose structured data such as contacts, call logs, SMS messages, and settings without requiring direct file system access.

entries.label: Device Screenshot Capture
entries.comment: The acquisition of a screenshot from a device screen. Contains the captured image (RasterPicture).

entries.label: Clock Offset Capture
entries.comment: The acquisition of a clock offset measurement from a device. Contains the ClockOffsetMeasurement recording the measured difference between the device clock and a reference time source.

entries.label: Acquisition Error Record
entries.comment: A record of an error encountered during data acquisition such as a bad sector, read timeout, I/O error, CRC error, or media surface damage.

entries.label: contains
entries.comment: The logical content encapsulated within the acquired data, such as bitstream data, files, or metadata.

entries.label: acquired from
entries.comment: The source from which the data was acquired, such as a device, device interface, or storage medium.

entries.label: stored in
entries.comment: The file or files in which the acquired data is physically stored (e.g., .E01 segment files, a .dd file, a backup archive).

entries.label: has info file
entries.comment: Links a RawImage to its accompanying RawImageInfoFile containing metadata.

entries.label: has acquisition error
entries.comment: Links a forensic image container or raw image info file to errors encountered during acquisition. Multiple errors can be recorded.

entries.label: contains error record
entries.comment: Links an AcquisitionRecordFile to the error records it contains.

entries.label: contains source hash
entries.comment: A hash value computed from the source device or media before or during acquisition.

entries.label: contains destination hash
entries.comment: A hash value computed from the acquired image or data after acquisition.

entries.label: embedded case number
entries.comment: The case number stored within the forensic image container metadata.

entries.label: embedded evidence number
entries.comment: The evidence number stored within the forensic image container metadata.

entries.label: embedded examiner name
entries.comment: The examiner name stored within the forensic image container metadata.

entries.label: embedded description
entries.comment: The description stored within the forensic image container metadata.

entries.label: embedded notes
entries.comment: The notes stored within the forensic image container metadata.

entries.label: backup format version
entries.comment: The version of the backup format used to produce the backup (e.g., iOS backup version 3.3, Android backup format v5).

entries.label: encrypted on generation
entries.comment: Whether the backup was encrypted at the time it was generated. A backup encrypted on generation may contain a richer dataset (e.g., iOS encrypted backups include keychain and health data) even if a decrypted copy is subsequently produced.

entries.label: is encrypted
entries.comment: Whether the backup is currently in an encrypted state. Used alongside encryptedOnGeneration to distinguish between a backup that is still encrypted and one that has been decrypted for analysis.

entries.label: contains start time
entries.comment: The acquisition start time as recorded in the acquisition record.

entries.label: contains end time
entries.comment: The acquisition end time as recorded in the acquisition record.

entries.label: error type
entries.comment: The type of acquisition error (e.g., bad sector, read timeout, I/O error, CRC error).

entries.label: error location start
entries.comment: The starting location of the error (e.g., sector number, byte offset).

entries.label: error location end
entries.comment: The ending location of the error (e.g., sector number, byte offset). If omitted, the error is at a single location.

entries.label: Keyword Search Result
entries.comment: A result from a keyword search operation during forensic analysis.

entries.label: Keyword Search Result Set
entries.comment: A collection of keyword search results from a search operation. Subsequent techniques may filter or reduce this set, for example by reviewing hits, discarding false positives, or redacting privileged content. Follows the same set-based pattern as FileSet and its subclasses.

entries.label: Keyword Index
entries.comment: An index of keywords created during forensic analysis.

entries.label: Keyword Indexing Configuration
entries.comment: Configuration settings used for keyword indexing during forensic analysis.

entries.label: has search result
entries.comment: Links a KeywordSearchResultSet to an individual KeywordSearchResult.

entries.label: has configuration
entries.comment: Links a KeywordIndex to its KeywordIndexingConfiguration.

entries.label: Timeline
entries.comment: A set of timeline entries extracted during forensic analysis.

entries.label: Timeline Entry
entries.comment: A single entry in a forensic timeline.

entries.label: Date Time Stamp
entries.comment: A timestamp observed in forensic analysis.

entries.label: Implicit Timing Information
entries.comment: A relative or implicit temporal indicator such as a sequence number, counter value, or ordering index, used when absolute timestamps are not available.

entries.label: Date Time Range
entries.comment: A time interval with start and end boundaries. Exactly one start property (inclusive or exclusive) and exactly one end property (inclusive or exclusive) must be specified. See SHACL shapes for validation.

entries.label: Clock Offset Measurement
entries.comment: The measured difference between a device clock and a reference time source. Records what was compared, the offset value, and when the comparison was made.

entries.label: Timestamp Offset
entries.comment: The computed difference between two timestamps, expressed in seconds. Positive values indicate the first timestamp is ahead of the second, negative values indicate it is behind.

entries.label: Sorted Timeline
entries.comment: A timeline whose entries have been ordered by position, as determined by a sorting process. Multiple entries may share the same position to indicate they are tied (indistinguishable in order).

entries.label: Sorted Timeline Entry
entries.comment: An intermediary node that associates a TimelineEntry with its ordinal position within a SortedTimeline. This allows the same TimelineEntry to exist in both an unsorted Timeline and a SortedTimeline without duplication.

entries.label: has timeline entry
entries.comment: Links a Timeline to its TimelineEntry instances.

entries.label: timeline entry value
entries.comment: The temporal value of this timeline entry - an absolute timestamp (DateTimeStamp), a time interval (DateTimeRange), or relative ordering (ImplicitTimingInformation).

entries.label: measured clock
entries.comment: The device or system whose clock was measured.

entries.label: reference time source
entries.comment: The reference time source used for comparison (e.g., NTP server, GPS time, examiner's calibrated watch).

entries.label: has sorted timeline entry
entries.comment: Links a sorted timeline to its sorted entry wrappers.

entries.label: references timeline entry
entries.comment: Links a sorted timeline entry to the original timeline entry it references.

entries.label: clock offset value
entries.comment: The clock offset value in seconds. Positive values indicate the clock is ahead, negative values indicate it is behind.

entries.label: clock offset known at
entries.comment: The specific point in time when this clock offset was determined.

entries.label: timestamp offset value
entries.comment: The difference between two timestamps in seconds. Positive values indicate the first timestamp is ahead of the second, negative values indicate it is behind.

entries.label: timestamp value
entries.comment: The date and time value of the timestamp.

entries.label: timestamp resolution
entries.comment: The precision or resolution of the timestamp (e.g., seconds, milliseconds, microseconds).

entries.label: timestamp timezone
entries.comment: The timezone of the timestamp.

entries.label: timing information value
entries.comment: The numeric value representing relative ordering or sequence.

entries.label: start time inclusive
entries.comment: The interval starts at this time (inclusive, i.e., >= this value).

entries.label: start time exclusive
entries.comment: The interval starts after this time (exclusive, i.e., > this value).

entries.label: end time inclusive
entries.comment: The interval ends at this time (inclusive, i.e., <= this value).

entries.label: end time exclusive
entries.comment: The interval ends before this time (exclusive, i.e., < this value).

entries.label: sort position
entries.comment: The ordinal position of this entry within its sorted timeline. Multiple entries may share the same position to indicate they are tied (indistinguishable in order).

entries.label: SQLite Database
entries.comment: A SQLite database file stored on disk.

entries.label: SQLite Table
entries.comment: A table within a SQLite database.

entries.label: SQLite Schema
entries.comment: The schema definition for a SQLite table.

entries.label: SQLite Field Definition
entries.comment: A column definition within a SQLite schema.

entries.label: SQLite Page
entries.comment: A physical storage page within a SQLite database file.

entries.label: SQLite Record
entries.comment: A record (row) within a SQLite table.

entries.label: SQLite Field
entries.comment: A field (cell) within a SQLite record.

entries.label: SQLite WAL
entries.comment: A Write-Ahead Log file associated with a SQLite database.

entries.label: SQLite WAL Frame
entries.comment: A single frame within a SQLite WAL, containing a version of a database page.

entries.label: SQLite Journal
entries.comment: A rollback journal file associated with a SQLite database, containing pre-modification page images.

entries.label: SQLite Journal Page Image
entries.comment: A stored copy of a database page as it existed before modification, held in the rollback journal.

entries.label: has table
entries.comment: Links a SQLite database to a table it contains.

entries.label: has page
entries.comment: Links a SQLite database to a physical storage page.

entries.label: has WAL
entries.comment: Links a SQLite database to its Write-Ahead Log.

entries.label: has journal
entries.comment: Links a SQLite database to its rollback journal.

entries.label: has schema
entries.comment: Links a SQLite table to its schema definition.

entries.label: has record
entries.comment: Links a SQLite table to a record it contains.

entries.label: has field definition
entries.comment: Links a SQLite schema to a column definition.

entries.label: has field
entries.comment: Links a SQLite record to a field it contains.

entries.label: recovered from page
entries.comment: The page from which this record was physically recovered. Deliberately has no rdfs:domain. Where bytes were found is a fact about them, true whether or not the reconstruction they support turns out to be correct, so it must be assertable of a solveit-analysis:HypothesisedRecord as readily as of an observed record. A domain of SQLiteRecord would not restrict that usage - rdfs:domain is an…

entries.label: defined by
entries.comment: Links a field value to its schema field definition.

entries.label: has blob content
entries.comment: Links to a CASE SQLiteBlob for binary field content. The binary content bytes are carried by a ContentDataFacet on the linked SQLiteBlob.

entries.label: contains data from
entries.comment: This page stores row data from the specified table.

entries.label: contains metadata from
entries.comment: This page stores B-tree structural metadata for the specified table.

entries.label: has child page
entries.comment: Links a B-tree interior page to its child pages.

entries.label: has frame
entries.comment: Links a WAL to a frame it contains.

entries.label: contains page version
entries.comment: Links a WAL frame to the page version it contains.

entries.label: has page image
entries.comment: Links a rollback journal to a page image it contains.

entries.label: original version of
entries.comment: Links a journal page image to the database page it represents the pre-modification state of.

entries.label: journal mode
entries.comment: The SQLite journal mode: DELETE, TRUNCATE, PERSIST, MEMORY, WAL, or OFF.

entries.label: field name
entries.comment: The column name in the schema.

entries.label: field type
entries.comment: The declared column type from the CREATE TABLE statement (e.g. TEXT, INTEGER, VARCHAR(20)). This may differ from the type affinity SQLite computes from it.

entries.label: field index
entries.comment: Zero-based position within the schema.

entries.label: is primary key
entries.comment: Whether this field is the primary key.

entries.label: page number
entries.comment: The page number within the database file.

entries.label: page type
entries.comment: e.g. b-tree leaf, b-tree interior, overflow, freelist.

entries.label: rowid
entries.comment: The rowid of this record within its table's B-tree. Omitted for records from WITHOUT ROWID tables.

entries.label: field content text
entries.comment: Text content of this field.

entries.label: field content integer
entries.comment: Integer content of this field.

entries.label: field content real
entries.comment: Real number content of this field.

entries.label: field content null
entries.comment: True if this field contains a NULL value.

entries.label: frame number
entries.comment: The sequence number of this frame within the WAL.

entries.label: frame page number
entries.comment: The database page number that this frame contains a version of.

entries.label: journal page number
entries.comment: The database page number this image is a pre-modification copy of.

entries.label: Tool Capability Profile
entries.comment: A declaration of what techniques a specific version of a tool can perform and what mitigations it implements, published by a named party. Distributed as a TTL file per tool version per publisher.

entries.label: SOLVE-IT Aware Instrument
entries.comment: A specialised tool that has been evaluated against SOLVE-IT tool capability profiles. Adds the consultedProfile property to link an instrument to the profiles used during mitigation assessment.

entries.label: Mitigation Capability
entries.comment: A declared capability that a specific mitigation is provided by a tool, optionally subject to conditions expressed as SHACL shapes.

entries.label: Condition Target Type
entries.comment: Enumeration of action components that conditions can evaluate against.

entries.label: profile for
entries.comment: Links to the tool that this profile describes. That tool object also potentially contains the tool version that this applies to.

entries.label: supports technique
entries.comment: Declares that the profiled tool supports a given technique.

entries.label: has mitigation capability
entries.comment: Links a profile to a mitigation capability declaration.

entries.label: consulted profile
entries.comment: Links an instrument to the capability profiles consulted during mitigation assessment.

entries.label: implements mitigation
entries.comment: The SOLVE-IT mitigation that this capability implements.

entries.label: applies when
entries.comment: A SHACL NodeShape defining the conditions for this mitigation to be active. Optional; if absent, the mitigation is unconditional.

entries.label: condition target
entries.comment: Specifies which component of the action the condition evaluates against. Required if appliesWhen is set.

entries.label: established for weakness
entries.comment: The weaknesses this capability was established against. One mitigation typically addresses many weaknesses, and a capability that names only its mitigation is read as covering all of them, including the ones the publisher never tested. Naming weaknesses here records what was actually established rather than what the mitigation could in principle address. There is no minimum: a capability naming…

entries.label: supporting citation
entries.comment: Evidence for this capability - a test report, a validation study, a published paper. The idiom here is that the profile mints its own Citation, carrying solveit-core:citationPlaintext or solveit-core:citationBibtex and omitting solveit-core:citationID, so a publisher can cite their own test report without it being registered in the DFCite series and the profile depends on nothing outside itself.…

entries.label: published by
entries.comment: The party that published this profile - a vendor, a testing programme, or a lab. An Identity rather than a name, for the reason hasCASEInputClass became an object property in 0.2.1: a party held in a string literal cannot be followed, cannot be shown to be the same party as one named elsewhere, and cannot be checked for a typo. Two profiles from one testing programme should be recognisable as…

entries.label: published date
entries.comment: When this profile was published.

entries.label: Weakness Evaluation
entries.comment: A risk assessment of a single SOLVE-IT weakness, capturing likelihood, impact, and optionally detectability ratings with computed scores.

entries.label: Weakness Evaluation Set
entries.comment: A collection of weakness evaluations scoped to a technique or context, with authorship and date metadata. Represents one assessment session.

entries.label: evaluates weakness
entries.comment: Links a weakness evaluation to the specific weakness being assessed.

entries.label: has evaluation
entries.comment: Links an evaluation set to its constituent weakness evaluations.

entries.label: scoped to technique
entries.comment: Optionally scopes an evaluation set to a specific technique context.

entries.label: evaluated by
entries.comment: The identity (person or organisation) that performed the evaluation.

entries.label: likelihood rating
entries.comment: The likelihood that this weakness will manifest. Integer score 1-3 (1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High).

entries.label: likelihood rationale
entries.comment: Justification for the assigned likelihood rating.

entries.label: impact rating
entries.comment: The impact if this weakness manifests. Integer score 1-3 (1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High).

entries.label: impact rationale
entries.comment: Justification for the assigned impact rating.

entries.label: detection difficulty rating
entries.comment: How difficult the weakness is to detect. Integer score 1-3 (1=Low/easy to detect, 2=Medium, 3=High/hard to detect).

entries.label: detection difficulty rationale
entries.comment: Justification for the assigned detection difficulty rating.

entries.label: likelihood x impact score
entries.comment: Computed score from Likelihood x Impact (range 1-9). Low=1, Medium=2, High=3.

entries.label: RPN score
entries.comment: Risk Priority Number: Likelihood x Impact x Detection Difficulty (range 1-27). Only present when detection difficulty is rated.

entries.label: evaluation context
entries.comment: Free-text context for the evaluation such as tool, platform, or case type.

entries.label: evaluation notes
entries.comment: Free-text rationale or caveats about the evaluation.

entries.label: evaluation set name
entries.comment: Descriptive label for the evaluation set.

entries.label: evaluation set description
entries.comment: Context or purpose of the evaluation set.

entries.label: evaluation date
entries.comment: Date when the assessment was performed.

entries.label: scoring scheme
entries.comment: The rating scheme the evaluations in this set were authored under: 'fi' (Frequency x Impact, ratings 1-3), 'fmea' (FMEA 3-point, ratings 1-3 with detection difficulty) or 'fmea6' (FMEA 6-point, ratings 1-6 with detection difficulty). Without it a consumer cannot tell a 3 that means 'high' on a three-point scale from a 3 that means 'moderate' on a six-point one, so the same integer describes two…

entries.label: DFT-1005: Search a crime scene for relevant physical evidence
entries.comment: The process of 'carefully documenting the conditions at a crime scene and identifying all relevant physical evidence.' (Birzer 2018).

entries.label: DFT-1006: Search a crime scene using digital sniffer dogs
entries.comment: The use of canines to locate obscured digital storage devices.

entries.label: DFT-1007: Detect the potential existence of digital devices using a SyncTriage-based approach
entries.comment: A technique developed in Hargreaves & Marshall (2018) whereby synchronization artifacts on a device are examined and used to identify the existence of a related device. Also sometimes used to infer activity that occurred on an inaccessible or unavailable device.

entries.label: DFT-1008: Detect the potential existence of digital devices by profiling network traffic
DFT-1009: Locate potential digital evidence sources via cloud account identifiers
DFT-1001: Triage devices or media
entries.comment: Digital forensic triage is a partial forensic examination conducted under (significant) time and resource constraints [DFCite-1115].

entries.label: DFT-1010: Place device in a faraday environment
entries.comment: Place a device in an environment designed to shield a mobile phone or small digital device from radio waves entering the environment and reaching the device, and to stop radio waves escaping from the environment (adapted from Lennox-Steele & Nisbet (2016))

entries.label: DFT-1011: Store seized devices or media in evidence bags
DFT-1012: Write protect storage media using a hardware write blocker
entries.comment: A hardware write blocking device [should] prevent any change to data in the user area of a hard drive while allowing access to all data on a hard drive. (Lyle 2006)

entries.label: DFT-1013: Write protect storage media using a software write blocker
entries.comment: Use of a software-based tool that prevents a computer from writing to computer storage media connected to it (NIST 2006)

entries.label: DFT-1114: Preserve memory contents via Cold Boot Attack
entries.comment: A precursor to extracting volatile memory (RAM) from a powered-off system by quickly rebooting or transferring the memory module to another system before residual data fades. Cooling the memory modules can significantly slow down data decay, preserving critical data such as encryption keys or passwords.

entries.label: DFT-1192: Disable connectivity using device configuration settings
entries.comment: This involves changing settings on a device to attempt to remove any connectivity options so that data cannot be sent or received over typical RF channels. This may involve multiple settings e.g. airplane mode and separate Bluetooth and WiFi toggles.

entries.label: DFT-1028: Physically remove a storage chip from a device (chip-off)
DFT-1029: Read data from a desoldered eMMC via a chip reader
DFT-1112: Locate and remove physical disks from a device
entries.comment: Locate the physical storage media inside a device and remove it, so that it can be connected to an examination system for acquisition.

entries.label: DFT-1113: Access internal storage via bootable environment
entries.comment: Booting the suspected computer device into an alternative operating system in order to image the attached disks.

entries.label: DFT-1166: Connect directly to storage media
entries.comment: This technique describes the occasions where it is necessary to connect directly to a disk without a hardware write blocker. This would typically then involve a subseqeunt software write blocker, which then presents a write protected interface.

entries.label: DFT-1171: Access a file system via live operating system
entries.comment: This involves accessing a live system and relying on the operating system's parsing of the file system to access files.

entries.label: DFT-1031: Recover encryption/decryption key from memory
entries.comment: This describes the technique whereby an attempt is made to extract key material from memory, or a memory acquisition of a running system to fascinate the decryption of some data

entries.label: DFT-1032: Recover encryption/decryption key information using side channel attacks
DFT-1033: Extract credential(s) from an accessible device to attempt access to a more secure device or service
entries.comment: Accessing a device with limited or no security to obtain a credential (e.g. password, PIN, token) that can be used to access another device or service.

entries.label: DFT-1034: Attack a stored credential or device using a brute force approach
entries.comment: A brute force attack, or exhaustive search is a password cracking approach where every combination of characters is tested until the correct one is found. This method is "guaranteed to work" given infinite time and resources which in a real-life scenario is not feasible.

entries.label: DFT-1035: Attack a stored credential or device using a dictionary-based approach
entries.comment: A dictionary attack is a password cracking technique where an attacker uses a list of passwords, called a dictionary, to attempt to guess a password.

entries.label: DFT-1036: Recover information about a potential device PIN or pattern lock using a smudge attack
DFT-1037: Obtain password from the device's owner
DFT-1038: Attack a stored credential or device using a rainbow table-based approach
DFT-1039: Downgrade apps to facilitate data extraction
entries.comment: Downgrading an app to a version in which data is available e.g. via a backup method

entries.label: DFT-1040: Exploit a mobile device to facilitate privileged access for data extraction
entries.comment: A process that typically exploits a security flaw in a specific device or operating system to enable users to perform higher privileged functions on a device (derived from Grover 2013)

entries.label: DFT-1041: Gain access to a device via a Pin2Pwn approach
DFT-1158: Configure device to enable a service needed for data extraction
entries.comment: Change a setting on a device such that a service needed for data extraction is enabled. This may require a user PIN that can be obtained using other techniques.

entries.label: DFT-1002: Copy sectors from storage media
entries.comment: Copying of sectors from a storage media, typically LBA~0~ to LBA~max~ to a bitstream that can be stored in a image format (DFT-1025).

entries.label: DFT-1003: Copy pages from physical memory
entries.comment: Involves creating a copy of the live memory data of a running system

entries.label: DFT-1004: Collect logical files selectively
entries.comment: Views a set of files (typically via direct access from previewing) and acquires a subset of them.

entries.label: DFT-1016: Collect specific pieces of information from a live running device
entries.comment: Running commands on a live system to collect specific pieces of information e.g. running processes or open ports

entries.label: DFT-1018: Collect data from a remote networked device
DFT-1020: Extract the file system from a mobile device
entries.comment: Accessing the file system(s) of the device and extracting a set of files (full or partial depending on level of access)

entries.label: DFT-1022: Capture mobile device screenshots (manually)
entries.comment: An examiner directly manipulates the target mobile device using the device's input interface (i.e., keypads and buttons), and records the content shown on the display of the device. (Fukami et al 2021)

entries.label: DFT-1023: Collect data from cloud service via a live web page using credentials
DFT-1024: Collect data from cloud service via submission of request to service provider
DFT-1030: Read data from unmanaged NAND
DFT-1104: Collect data using open source intelligence
DFT-1111: Record system clock offset
entries.comment: Recording a system clock compared with trusted time source

entries.label: DFT-1157: Extract device data using exposed service
entries.comment: Use an exposed service on a device to extract data. This represents several of the mobile data extraction methods e.g. Query content providers (android), AFC (iOS).

entries.label: DFT-1159: Extract mobile data via deployed agent
entries.comment: Deploy software to a mobile device that can carry out some function, either collect data with available permissions or attempt further exploitation e.g. sandbox escape.

entries.label: DFT-1160: Collect data with 'cloud backup restore' approach
entries.comment: Restore a device's cloud backup to a donor device, then subsequently use a local acquisition approach on that donor device, e.g. T1019/T1020

entries.label: DFT-1161: Collect data from cloud service via API using credentials
entries.comment: Copying data from a cloud service using the officially supported API of the provider.

entries.label: DFT-1162: Read data from a device via In-System Programming (ISP)
DFT-1163: Capture mobile device screenshots (automatically)
entries.comment: Programmatically controlling a mobile device while capturing screenshots of the display.

entries.label: DFT-1164: Read data directly from a block device
entries.comment: Rather than imaging a block device, this involves accessing it directly without the expectation of saving block data to a forensic image format.

entries.label: DFT-1175: Extract data from an Android device using content queries
entries.comment: Use of content queries on Android devices via adb to extract specific pieces of data exposed by content providers.

entries.label: DFT-1198: Compute hash of data read from source device
entries.comment: Process data accessed on a source device (e.g. attached disk or other media) and compute the cryptographic hash of the data

entries.label: DFT-1025: Store bitstream data in a forensic image format
entries.comment: Storage of bitstream data recovered from a digital device

entries.label: DFT-1026: Store data in standard archive format
entries.comment: Storing acquired data in a standard archive format such as rar, tar or zip

entries.label: DFT-1178: Store bitstream data in a raw image format
entries.comment: Storage of bitstream data recovered from a digital device as raw files.

entries.label: DFT-1208: Store acquisition metadata along with a forensic image format
entries.comment: Records details such as case and examiner details, and the acquisition hash, with a forensic image container alongside the bitstream data or logical files.

entries.label: DFT-1042: Verify hash of copied data matches the hash of the data read from source device
entries.comment:
Compares a hash of data read from a source device with a hash computed by reading back the copy of that data stored in a raw image or a forensic image container. 

The source hash may be computed as the data is read during imaging, or by reading the source device again at a later point. 

What distinguishes this technique is that the reference hash comes from reading the source device, rather…

entries.label: DFT-1043: Read bitstream from forensic image container file(s)
entries.comment: The decoding of a forensic format such as EWF such that the raw sectors can be accessed by a forensic tool (typically performed on-the-fly internally in a tool.)

entries.label: DFT-1044: Decode data stored in a mobile backup format
entries.comment: Processing an extracted mobile device backup to access the files contained within.

entries.label: DFT-1045: Read contents from standard archive file(s)
entries.comment: Extract files from a common archive format e.g. TAR, RAR, ZIP

entries.label: DFT-1102: Decode data extracted from unmanaged NAND
DFT-1170: Read contents from logical forensic container file(s)
entries.comment: Decodes logical image formats such as L01, AD1, CTR, or AFF4-L. The output here is not an image file but rather a set of files and their metadata.

entries.label: DFT-1172: Read bitstream from raw image file(s)
entries.comment: This technique reads data from a raw image e.g. a dd image.

entries.label: DFT-1173: Extract data from captured screenshots
entries.comment: Processing a screenshot captured from a device to extract data for further processing.

entries.label: DFT-1174: Read evidential files stored directly on local file system
entries.comment: Represents reading files that have been acquired or extracted directly to the local file system.

entries.label: DFT-1193: Read metadata from within a forensic image container
entries.comment: The processes of reading the metadata values stored within forensic container formats

entries.label: DFT-1199: Compute hash of stored bitstream data
entries.comment: Cryptographically hashing either data exposed directly from a raw image or a decompressed physical image from a container format.

entries.label: DFT-1204: Verify hash of stored bitstream data matches a stored hash
entries.comment: Compares a hash computed over stored bitstream data against a recorded hash, to assess whether the stored data has changed since it was written.

entries.label: DFT-1046: Redact digital forensic tool results to protect privileged material
DFT-1047: Filter files using a hashset to reduce files examined
entries.comment: After hashing a set of files, compare the hashes against a known hashset to identify and remove known files from further examination.

entries.label: DFT-1048: Protect privacy by only partially processing data from a source
entries.comment: Limiting the scope of file processing based on type, date or other criteria to protect privacy.

entries.label: DFT-1059: Identify partitions
entries.comment: Partitions are defined as ‘allocated contiguous sets of sectors from storage media’. This involves recovering the list of partitions that exist on a storage media.

entries.label: DFT-1060: Enumerate allocated files and folders
entries.comment: This involves parsing the allocated file system data structures and reconstructing the file system of the target media or device.

entries.label: DFT-1061: Recover non-allocated files
entries.comment: The recovery of files from non-allocated space

entries.label: DFT-1062: Decrypt encrypted file systems/volumes
entries.comment: The process of decrypting an encrypted file system/volume to make its contents accessible for analysis.

entries.label: DFT-1063: Identify file types
entries.comment: Applying a process that identifies the types of files.

entries.label: DFT-1168: Identify volumes
entries.comment: From a partition or data from a full disk, identify volumes.

entries.label: DFT-1065: Extract artifacts from operating system-level content indexer(s)
entries.comment: Examine information from operating system artifacts relating to content indexing and search capabilities e.g. Windows Desktop Search

entries.label: DFT-1066: Extract artifacts from operating system log files
DFT-1067: Extract artifacts from operating system cloud synchronization features
entries.comment: Focuses on operating system level cloud syncronization features, such as iCloud Drive and OneDrive, which may be used to synchronize files between a local system and a cloud service.

entries.label: DFT-1068: Extract operating system artifacts indicating recently used files
entries.comment: The process of examining operating system files to extract artifacts that may indicate file accesses.

entries.label: DFT-1083: Extract artifacts from operating system memory structures
entries.comment: Examination of the operating system structures that allows individual processes to be listed and pages used by specific processes to be enumerated.

entries.label: DFT-1096: Extract operating system artifacts indicating program execution
entries.comment: The process of examining operating system files to extract artifacts that may indicate a program has been run.

entries.label: DFT-1097: Extract operating system artifacts indicating installed software
entries.comment: Extraction and analysis of information that allows programs installed on an OS to be identified.

entries.label: DFT-1098: Enumerate operating system user accounts
entries.comment: Examination of operating system artifacts to determine user accounts

entries.label: DFT-1116: Extract references to connected devices
entries.comment: Examine artifacts and extract indicators of devices that have been connected to the target device.

entries.label: DFT-1149: Extract artifacts from the file versioning feature
entries.comment: Extraction of data from the versioning system used by an operating system to store older versions of files.

entries.label: DFT-1180: Extract file(s) from a pre-deletion container
entries.comment: An examination of the operating system structures that represent the 'pre-deletion' container (i.e. Recycle Bin/Trash) to extract those files and potentially additional metadata such as original path or date it was moved.

entries.label: DFT-1185: Extract data from operating system notifications
entries.comment: Recovery of the notifications produced by applications that are stored by the operating system.

entries.label: DFT-1190: Extract operating system version(s) from data source
entries.comment: The process of extracting and processing the artifacts that describe the current operating system version and associated version details e.g. build, service pack etc.

entries.label: DFT-1196: Extract operating system installation date
entries.comment: Extract the date and time recorded as the installation date of the operating system.

entries.label: DFT-1197: Determine mount point mappings within an operating system
entries.comment: This involves establishing what mount points (including drive letters) within an operating system are mapped to, either a partition or device.

entries.label: DFT-1069: Extract artifacts from a web browser
entries.comment: Recovery of information left from web browsing activity (derived from Oh et al (2011))

entries.label: DFT-1070: Extract artifacts from email client(s) or webmail access
DFT-1072: Extract artifacts from chat app(s)
entries.comment: Analysis of the files that provide the backing store for a chat or messenger application

entries.label: DFT-1073: Extract artifacts from calendar app(s)
DFT-1074: Extract artifacts from social network app(s)
DFT-1075: Extract artifacts from maps/travel app(s)
DFT-1077: Extract artifacts from photo management app(s)
DFT-1078: Extract artifacts from cloud synchronization app(s)
entries.comment: Involves examination of cloud synchronization artifacts from apps rather than those built into the operating system.

entries.label: DFT-1105: Examine memory dump from an application
entries.comment: Examination of the specific structures from the memory of a specific application

entries.label: DFT-1107: Extract artifacts from health/fitness app(s)
DFT-1108: Extract artifacts from reminders app(s)
DFT-1109: Extract artifacts from payment app(s)
DFT-1133: Extract artifacts from AI companion app(s)
entries.comment: The forensic examination of the artifacts describing the configuration or the interaction with an AI companion app or service.

entries.label: DFT-1177: Extract artifacts from multiplayer game app(s)
entries.comment: Extracting artifacts from multiplayer gaming apps.

entries.label: DFT-1179: Extract artifacts from drone/UAV app(s)
entries.comment: The examination of a mobile app used to control Unmanned Areial Vehicles (UAVs) or 'drones'.

entries.label: DFT-1181: Extract artifacts from smart home app(s)
entries.comment: Examine the data stored by an app designed to control, monitor or program smart home capabilities.

entries.label: DFT-1071: Extract data from SQLite database(s)
