entries.comment: Examination of a SQLite database file(s) to extract information from within.

entries.label: DFT-1099: Repair a damaged or incomplete file using `grafting`
entries.comment: Repair file by grafting different reference data onto fragment(s)

entries.label: DFT-1100: Extract metadata from within images
entries.comment: The extraction of metadata from within images (pictures). e.g. EXIF, XMP. IPTC, iTXt etc.

entries.label: DFT-1167: Extract search terms from URLs
entries.comment: Parsing a URL and extracting search terms from the parameters.

entries.label: DFT-1187: Extract content from compound files
entries.comment: The process of extracting files and objects contained within compound files, including archives, Office documents, PDFs, and email containers, surfacing the contained items as first-class files for further analysis.

entries.label: DFT-1191: Parse allocated structures in Windows HIVE files
entries.comment: Enumerate the allocated structures within HIVE files (typically Windows Registry) to extract the tree structure along with keys and their values.

entries.label: DFT-1205: Decode raw data into data value(s)
entries.comment: The process of interpreting a sequence of bytes as a typed value, such as a number, a string, or a date, under an assumed encoding.

entries.label: DFT-1206: Decode a number from raw data
entries.comment: The process of interpreting a sequence of bytes as a numeric value under an assumed width, signedness, and byte order.

entries.label: DFT-1207: Decode a string from raw data
entries.comment: The process of decoding a sequence of bytes as text under an assumed character encoding.

entries.label: DFT-1021: Extract artifacts from a configuration file
entries.comment: Examination of a file that was designed for storing configuration information for a piece of software (e.g. an application or operating system feature)

entries.label: DFT-1052: Generate timeline
entries.comment: The extraction and normalisation of timestamps from a data source into a set of timeline entries

entries.label: DFT-1053: Extract 'entities' from a data source
entries.comment: Extracting common types of entity in a data source e.g. email addresses, IP addresses, domain names, URLs, credit card numbers, etc.

entries.label: DFT-1056: Enumerate connections between artifacts
entries.comment: Finds references between artifacts, such as operating system artifacts that refer to a specific file

entries.label: DFT-1076: Extract artifacts from log files
entries.comment: Examination of a file that was designed for incremental logging from a piece of software (e.g. an application or operating system feature)

entries.label: DFT-1120: Extract artifacts from app data automatically
entries.comment: The use of automation to extract pieces of data that are potentially useful for a digital forensic investigation from app data.

entries.label: DFT-1121: Index a data source for keyword searching
entries.comment: Extracting strings from a data source and adding them to an index for subsequent searching.

entries.label: DFT-1165: Extract software configuration information
entries.comment: Examination of one or more files to extract configuration information for a piece of software.

entries.label: DFT-1169: Filter files related to an application
entries.comment: This technique takes a set of files and determines which are related to a specified application.

entries.label: DFT-1186: Compute per-file hash values
entries.comment: The process of computing one or more hash digests for each file in a set, producing per-file digests that can subsequently be used for matching, deduplication, or integrity comparison.

entries.label: DFT-1209: Extract artifacts from data provided by a service provider
entries.comment: Parse data supplied by an online service provider into artifacts such as messages, accounts, contacts and events.

entries.label: DFT-1049: Keyword search
entries.comment: This technique involves searching data in the case for specific strings

entries.label: DFT-1050: Locate relevant files using a hashset to identify files of interest
DFT-1051: Locate potentially relevant files using fuzzy hash matching
DFT-1086: Analyze timeline
entries.comment: The process of searching, filtering, sorting, highlighting, or aggregating timeline entries to determine which are relevant for event reconstruction, or to identify times of interest (adapted from Breitinger et al. 2025)

entries.label: DFT-1118: Locate relevant files by path
entries.comment: Use the path of file name to determine potential relevance of the file.

entries.label: DFT-1203: Use an AI-based prompt for interrogating case data
entries.comment: Using an AI-based chat interface to query the data within a case.

entries.label: DFT-1054: Review artifacts or content manually for relevant material
entries.comment: Manual examination of files or artifacts to determine their relevance to the investigation.

entries.label: DFT-1055: Examine file and folder structure
entries.comment: The process of examining the directory hierarchy, file and folder names (rather than file contents) to identify potentially relevant material.

entries.label: DFT-1057: Search for indicators of steganography
entries.comment: Searching for the presence of current or historical steganography software on a system

entries.label: DFT-1058: Search for mismatched file extensions
entries.comment: Checking the content of a file against its file extension to identify mismatches.

entries.label: DFT-1128: Search for indicators of malware
entries.comment: Searching for the presence of current or historical malware on a system

entries.label: DFT-1129: Search for indicators of clock tampering
entries.comment: Searching for indicators that the system clock has been tampered with

entries.label: DFT-1130: Search for indicators of encrypted data
entries.comment: Searching for the presence of current or historical encrypted data on a system

entries.label: DFT-1131: Search for indicators of trail obfuscation
entries.comment: Searching for the presence of current or historical trail obfuscation on a system

entries.label: DFT-1132: Search for indicators of artifact wiping
entries.comment: Searching for the presence of current or historical artifact wiping

entries.label: DFT-1084: Extract potentially user-identifying content from account information
entries.comment: Analysis of user account information to extract content that may help identify the person associated with an account, such as usernames, real names, password hints, security questions, recovery email addresses, and profile details.

entries.label: DFT-1085: Conflate specific account identifiers to a single user identity
DFT-1103: Virtualize suspect system for previewing
entries.comment: A suspect disk image can be configured to boot as a virtual machine, which allows screenshots to be taken showing how the user's desktop looked for example.

entries.label: DFT-1115: Visualize geolocation information
entries.comment: Presenting points or paths visually using extracted data, typically on a map

entries.label: DFT-1089: Review source code of software
entries.comment: Typically to  understand it's capabilities, the artifacts it produces, or what user actions could be potentially reconstructed

entries.label: DFT-1090: Experiment with software to ascertain forensic artifacts
entries.comment: The process of running software in a controlled environment to observe its behavior and identify potential forensic artifacts.

entries.label: DFT-1095: Instrument a piece of running software
entries.comment: This can be done during experiments to help ascertain functionality, or potential forensic artifacts

entries.label: DFT-1101: Conduct cell site survey
entries.comment: Taking measurements to assess which cells actually provide service at a specific location (adapted from Tart et al 2012).

entries.label: DFT-1119: Automatically scan for artifact changes caused by app updates
entries.comment: Monitor every version change of an application to determine if there are changes to the way the app stores data

entries.label: DFT-1087: Reconstruct the location-based properties of an event
entries.comment: The process of assigning location properties to a reconstructed event

entries.label: DFT-1088: Reconstruct relations between events or properties of events
entries.comment: The process of determining the existence and nature of relationships between entities during event reconstruction

entries.label: DFT-1117: Reconstruct the time that an event may have occurred
entries.comment: The process of assigning a time component to a reconstructed event

entries.label: DFT-1154: Reconstruct an identity associated with an event
entries.comment: The process of attempting to link an identity (account, person etc.) to a reconstructed event

entries.label: DFT-1155: Reconstruct that a specific event may have occurred
entries.comment: The process of reconstructing that an operation occurred on a digital system

entries.label: DFT-1156: Reconstruct if an event could have functionally occurred on a system given its capabilities
entries.comment: Reconstructing the configuration or capabilities of a system at the time of an event

entries.label: DFT-1195: Generate Alternative Hypotheses
entries.comment: The process of considering what are the alternative possibilities (other than the proposed hypothesis) for the digital forensic artifacts/traces that we are observing

entries.label: DFT-1200: Evaluate observations in light of hypotheses
entries.comment: The process of assessing the probability or strength of the observations under each of two or more competing hypotheses, and expressing the strength of support for one over another.

entries.label: DFT-1202: Verify automated results manually
entries.comment: The process of manually reviewing the results from an automated process and checking the results are correct.

entries.label: DFT-1014: Document the chain of custody
entries.comment: A process that tracks the movement of evidence through its collection, safeguarding, and analysis lifecycle by documenting each person who handled the evidence, the date/time it was collected or transferred, and the purpose for the transfer [DFCite-1147].

entries.label: DFT-1091: Tag artifacts
entries.comment: Make a record of selected files or pieces of data so they can be accessed easily, or used for generating automated reports.

entries.label: DFT-1092: Generate tag-based automated report
entries.comment: Generate a report in PDF, HTML or other format that compiles tagged (or bookmarked) items from a case into a package that can be reviewed.

entries.label: DFT-1094: Disclose investigation material to an authorized legal authority
DFT-1210: Obtain approval for a digital forensic activity
entries.comment: Obtain the legal or organisational authorisation required before a digital forensic activity can be carried out, e.g. a search warrant, production order or internal sign-off.

entries.label: DFT-1015: Collect logical files selectively based on privacy preserving criteria
entries.comment: Previewing a data source and selecting a subset of the data for collection into a container such as a tar/zip file or a forensic image format for the purposes of protecting the privacy of the complainant or witness.

entries.label: DFT-1019: Extract a backup from a mobile device
entries.comment: Using the in-built backup capability of a device to extract a subset of its contents

entries.label: DFT-1027: Read data from a device using JTAG
DFT-1122: Keyword search (case-type wordlists)
entries.comment: Searching for case-type specific keywords

entries.label: DFT-1123: Keyword search (case-specific wordlists)
entries.comment: Searching for case-specific keywords, e.g. people's names, places etc.

entries.label: DFT-1124: Keyword search (indexed)
entries.comment: Searching for keywords within a generated index of data in a case

entries.label: DFT-1125: Keyword search (live)
entries.comment: Searching for keywords over the raw data in a case without using an index of text content

entries.label: DFT-1126: Keyword search (live) (physical)
entries.comment: Searching for keywords over the raw data on a sector by sector basis

entries.label: DFT-1127: Keyword search (live) (logical)
entries.comment: Searching for keywords over the raw data, without an index of text content, but on a file by file basis

entries.label: DFT-1151: Keyword search (over extracted artifacts)
entries.comment: Keyword searching only applied over extracted artifacts

entries.label: DFT-1153: Apply offset to a timestamp
entries.comment: Application of a time offset to a timestamp

entries.label: DFT-1064: Carve non-allocated files
entries.comment: The process of recovering files from non-allocated space using only the structural properties of files.

entries.label: DFT-1150: Recover non-allocated files using residual file metadata
entries.comment: Use metadata that remains in the file system to recover non-allocated files

entries.label: DFT-1137: Extract browser history artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of the history component of a web browser.

entries.label: DFT-1138: Extract browser cache artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of the content saved locally by browsers to improve performance

entries.label: DFT-1139: Extract browser session artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of sessions and open tabs and their individual histories

entries.label: DFT-1140: Extract browser autofill artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of data that is stored to autocomplete entries in forms

entries.label: DFT-1141: Extract browser bookmark artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of the links saved within a browser to facilitate quick access

entries.label: DFT-1142: Extract browser download artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of records of files downloaded with a browser

entries.label: DFT-1143: Extract browser configuration artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of a browsers configuration

entries.label: DFT-1144: Enumerate browser profiles
entries.comment: The enumeration of the separate user profiles set up within a browser

entries.label: DFT-1145: Extract browser extensions artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of the extensions installed within a browser

entries.label: DFT-1146: Extract browser synchronization artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of the settings and artifacts resulting from a browser synchronization feature

entries.label: DFT-1147: Extract browser cookie artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of stored browser cookies

entries.label: DFT-1148: Extract browser web storage artifacts
entries.comment: The examination of

entries.label: DFT-1194: Classify if audio is potentially synthetically generated
entries.comment: Classification of audio with respect to its origin, i.e., whether it is synthetically generated (e.g. text-to-speech synthesis or voice conversion) or naturally captured from a live speaker.

entries.label: DFT-1106: Classify if a video is potentially synthetically generated
DFT-1176: Classify if an image is potentially synthetically generated
entries.comment: Classification of images with respect to their origin, i.e., whether they are synthetically generated or naturally captured by a camera.

entries.label: DFT-1134: Use time anchors to estimate clock offset
entries.comment: Correlate timestamps from the system clock and an external trusted time source (Time Anchoring)

entries.label: DFT-1182: Filter a timeline for relevant entries
entries.comment: Provide some criteria that selects only a subset of timeline entries from a set.

entries.label: DFT-1184: Sort a timeline so entries are ordered chronologically
entries.comment: Order a timeline based on the values in the timestamp entry.

entries.label: CAC Investigation
entries.comment: A child-protection investigation that follows a standard action lifecycle that commonly begins with the discovery of CSAM, the receipt of a cybertip, or a call to a hotline. This class extends the CASE Investigation class to provide CAC-specific investigation capabilities with gUFO Object modeling.

entries.label: Initial Investigation Phase
entries.comment: Initial phase of CAC investigation involving cybertip receipt and preliminary review.

entries.label: Analysis Phase
entries.comment: Phase focused on detailed analysis of evidence and cybertip information.

entries.label: Legal Process Phase
entries.comment: Phase involving legal processes such as search warrants and subpoenas.

entries.label: Evidence Phase
entries.comment: Phase focused on evidence collection, analysis, and curation.

entries.label: Victim Phase
entries.comment: Phase focused on victim identification, rescue, and support. Deprecated: consider using the more specific VictimIdentificationPhase, VictimRescuePhase, VictimSupportPhase, or VictimRecoveryPhase classes.

entries.label: Conclusion Phase
entries.comment: Final phase involving case closure or prosecution referral.

entries.label: Investigation Lifecycle Situation
entries.comment: Overall situation encompassing the complete CAC investigation lifecycle.

entries.label: Receive Cybertip Action
entries.comment: The initial action of receiving a cybertip report from a reporting entity (e.g., NCMEC, INHOPE).

entries.label: Review Cybertip Action
entries.comment: The action of reviewing and analyzing a cybertip report by an analyst.

entries.label: Legal Process Action
entries.comment: The action of initiating legal processes such as search warrants, subpoenas, or MLAT requests.

entries.label: Evidence Review Action
entries.comment: The action of reviewing and analyzing digital evidence using forensic tools.

entries.label: CSAM Curation Action
entries.comment: The action of curating and classifying child sexual abuse material using standard classification systems.

entries.label: Victim Rescue Action
entries.comment: The action of rescuing and providing support to identified victims.

entries.label: Unknown Victim Submission
entries.comment: The action of submitting information about unidentified victims to relevant databases.

entries.label: Child Sexual Abuse Event
entries.comment: A class representing any event involving child sexual abuse or exploitation. This is the base class for all CAC incidents modeled as gUFO Event. Victim and offender ages at the time of the event SHOULD be represented using cacontology-temporal:AgeAtTimeSituation instances rather than static age literals to support age-of-consent, Romeo-and-Juliet, and other temporal legal analyses.

entries.label: Child Sexual Abuse Material Incident
entries.comment: Incidents involving possession, manufacture, or distribution of child sexual abuse material. This replaces the deprecated 'ChildPornographyIncident' term.

entries.label: Digitally Generated CSAM Incident
entries.comment: Incidents involving digitally generated or manipulated child sexual abuse material.

entries.label: Live Streaming Child Sexual Abuse
entries.comment: Incidents involving live streaming of child sexual abuse.

entries.label: Grooming and Solicitation
entries.comment: Incidents involving grooming or solicitation of children for sexual purposes.

entries.label: Sextortion
entries.comment: Incidents involving sexual extortion of children.

entries.label: Victim Role
entries.comment: Role of a person who is a victim of child sexual abuse or exploitation. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Role. When the victim's age is known at the time of a specific event or phase, it SHOULD be captured via one or more cacontology-temporal:AgeAtTimeSituation instances linked to the underlying person.

entries.label: Offender Role
entries.comment: Role of a person who commits child sexual abuse or exploitation. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Role. When offender age or age-gap reasoning is relevant (e.g., Romeo-and-Juliet scenarios), age SHOULD be represented via cacontology-temporal:AgeAtTimeSituation instances for the corresponding person.

entries.label: Rescuer Role
entries.comment: Role of a person involved in rescuing or protecting victims (e.g., law enforcement, NGO worker). Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Role.

entries.label: Investigator Role
entries.comment: Role of law enforcement officer or analyst conducting CAC investigation. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Role.

entries.label: Analyst Role
entries.comment: Role of professional analyzing cybertips and digital evidence. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Role.

entries.label: Conspiracy to Commit Child Sexual Abuse
entries.comment: Criminal conspiracy involving multiple defendants coordinating child sexual abuse or exploitation activities (e.g., 8-defendant Brooklyn trafficking ring).

entries.label: Criminal Enterprise
entries.comment: Organized criminal group conducting systematic child exploitation activities with defined roles and structure.

entries.label: Coordinated Offense Pattern
entries.comment: Pattern of coordinated criminal activities involving multiple perpetrators working together across time and locations.

entries.label: Multi-Defendant Indictment
entries.comment: Legal indictment involving multiple defendants in coordinated criminal enterprise (e.g., 19-count superseding indictment).

entries.label: Conspiracy Role
entries.comment: Role of individual within criminal conspiracy.

entries.label: Conspiracy Leader Role
entries.comment: Leadership role within criminal conspiracy, directing and coordinating activities.

entries.label: Conspiracy Member Role
entries.comment: Member role within criminal conspiracy, participating in coordinated activities.

entries.label: Subject
entries.comment: Continuity alias for the investigation-subject role. Deprecated in favor of case-investigation:Subject (a uco-role:Role whose conduct is within the scope of an investigation); new graphs should use the CASE class directly.

entries.label: has phase begin point
entries.comment: Temporal begin point for investigation phase.

entries.label: has phase end point
entries.comment: Temporal end point for investigation phase.

entries.label: has role begin point
entries.comment: Temporal begin point for CAC role.

entries.label: has role end point
entries.comment: Temporal end point for CAC role.

entries.label: phase duration
entries.comment: Duration of investigation phase.

entries.label: severity level
entries.comment: The severity level of an incident (0-3, mapping to NorRating/EUROPOL scales).

entries.label: investigation status
entries.comment: Current status of CAC investigation (active, suspended, closed, referred).

entries.label: phase progress
entries.comment: Progress percentage within current investigation phase (0.0-1.0).

entries.label: conspiracy member count
entries.comment: Number of individuals involved in criminal conspiracy (e.g., 8 defendants).

entries.label: indictment counts
entries.comment: Number of criminal counts in indictment (e.g., 19 counts in superseding indictment).

entries.label: conspiracy duration
entries.comment: Duration of criminal conspiracy from start to disruption.

entries.label: case number
entries.comment: Court or agency case identifier for an investigation or proceeding (e.g., PACER docket number '3:20-cr-00029-SLG-MMS'). Declared as a subproperty of uco-core:externalIdentifier so consumers inherit UCO identifier semantics; the richer canonical pattern uco-core:externalReference remains available for fully-qualified references.

entries.label: jurisdiction
entries.comment: Legal authority scope of an investigation, proceeding, agency, or action (e.g., 'federal', 'E.D. Wis.', 'Victoria, Australia'). Declared once at core level to consolidate the per-module string variants; for structured jurisdictional entities use cacontology-multi:Jurisdiction and its subclasses.

entries.label: has step
entries.comment: Links a CAC investigation to each ordered step in its lifecycle.

entries.label: next step
entries.comment: Denotes the chronologically next action in the lifecycle.

entries.label: previous step
entries.comment: Denotes the chronologically previous action in the lifecycle.

entries.label: has phase
entries.comment: Links investigation to its current or historical phases.

entries.label: transitions to
entries.comment: Links one investigation phase to the next phase in sequence.

entries.label: targets service
entries.comment: Links a legal process action to the digital service it targets.

entries.label: legal instrument
entries.comment: Links a legal process action to its legal instrument (e.g., search warrant, subpoena).

entries.label: uses classification
entries.comment: Links a CSAM curation action to the classification system used.

entries.label: rescued victim
entries.comment: Links a victim rescue action to the rescued victim.

entries.label: has age situation
entries.comment: Links a person to an Age At Time Situation that attributes a concrete age value to them over a time-bounded interval. This is the primary bridge from identity data into the gUFO-based age modeling pattern.

entries.label: has victim age situation
entries.comment: Convenience link from a child sexual abuse event to an Age At Time Situation describing the victim’s age at or during that event. Implementations MAY infer or materialize this from person-level age situations and event timepoints.

entries.label: has offender age situation
entries.comment: Convenience link from a child sexual abuse event to an Age At Time Situation describing the offender’s age at or during that event, enabling age-gap and Romeo-and-Juliet style analyses.

entries.label: submitted to
entries.comment: Links an unknown victim submission to the target database.

entries.label: involves victim
entries.comment: Links an event to a victim role.

entries.label: involves offender
entries.comment: Links an event to an offender role.

entries.label: uses channel
entries.comment: Links an event to a digital service or communication channel.

entries.label: produces artifact
entries.comment: Links an event to a digital artifact it produces.

entries.label: occurs during phase
entries.comment: Links an action to the investigation phase during which it occurs.

entries.label: depicts child
entries.comment: Links a digital artifact to a child depicted in it.

entries.label: current phase
entries.comment: The current active phase of the investigation.

entries.label: participates in conspiracy
entries.comment: Links individual to conspiracy they participate in.

entries.label: leads conspiracy
entries.comment: Links individual to conspiracy they lead or direct.

entries.label: results in indictment
entries.comment: Links conspiracy to indictment resulting from investigation.

entries.label: located at
entries.comment: Direct edge from an entity to a location. UCO idiom alternatives: uco-core:Relationship with kindOfRelationship 'Located_At', or uco-action:location for Actions; this property supports direct edges where a reified Relationship is unnecessary.

entries.label: participates in event
entries.comment: Links a participant (person, role, or organization) to an event they take part in. Referenced by cacontology-core-shapes SPARQL constraints; declared here to close the declaration gap (Issue #41).

entries.label: Entity
entries.comment: The most general class in the CAC semantic spine. All CAC domain concepts should anchor to one of its subclasses.

entries.label: Enduring Entity
entries.comment: A thing that persists through time while potentially changing state. This is the CAC-facing root for all object-like entities including people, organizations, devices, artifacts, places, and assessment results.

entries.label: Person-Like Entity
entries.comment: An enduring entity that is person-like in the domain model. Use for natural persons and person-profile abstractions.

entries.label: Organization-Like Entity
entries.comment: An enduring entity that represents an organization, institution, team, agency, or other collectively organized actor.

entries.label: Digital System Entity
entries.comment: An enduring entity representing a software or system-level resource such as an online service platform, moderation system, or digital environment.

entries.label: Artifact
entries.comment: An enduring entity that is inspectable, storable, transferable, or evidentiary. Aligned to UCO ObservableObject for digital evidence interoperability.

entries.label: Place-Like Entity
entries.comment: An enduring entity used to represent places, venues, virtual environments treated as locatable contexts, or place-like reference points.

entries.label: Assessment Result
entries.comment: An output or conclusion of some evaluative, analytic, classification, or decision-making process. Intentionally not subclassed from uco-observable:ObservableObject because the semantic identity of a result is the assessment outcome, not the artifact that stores it.

entries.label: Occurrent
entries.comment: A CAC organizing superclass for things that happen or unfold in time. This is a CAC-layer abstraction not directly mapped to a gUFO superclass in the base spine.

entries.label: Event
entries.comment: Something that happens or unfolds in time — an action, interaction, incident, hearing, or process step.

entries.label: Exploitation Event
entries.comment: An event representing an act of exploitation, abuse, or victimization of a child.

entries.label: Detection Event
entries.comment: An event representing the detection, identification, or flagging of content, behavior, or indicators relevant to child exploitation.

entries.label: Coordination Event
entries.comment: An event representing coordination, information sharing, or collaborative activity among stakeholders.

entries.label: Support Event
entries.comment: An event representing victim support, advocacy, training, or welfare-related activity.

entries.label: Legal Event
entries.comment: An event representing a legal proceeding, judicial action, sentencing hearing, or other court-related occurrence.

entries.label: Investigative Action
entries.comment: An event that is specifically an investigative action within a CAC investigation. Aligned to both CASE InvestigativeAction and UCO Action for investigation interoperability.

entries.label: Situation
entries.comment: A context, state, or configuration that holds at a time and may involve multiple participants. Aligned to gUFO Situation.

entries.label: Role
entries.comment: A non-rigid role borne by an enduring entity in a certain relational or contextual setting. A bearer can gain or lose a role without ceasing to exist. Aligned to both gUFO Role and UCO Role.

entries.label: Phase
entries.comment: A temporal stage of some enduring entity, process, or situation. The bearer remains the same entity while changing phase. Aligned to gUFO Phase.

entries.label: Conditioning Phase
entries.comment: Temporal phase in which an offender shapes victim readiness, situational constraints, or compliance preparatory to the primary exploitation act — through rapport, deception, isolation, normalization, desensitization, dependency, or compliance training.

entries.label: conditioning mode
entries.comment: Dominant mechanism through which conditioning is accomplished in a documented offense phase instance.

entries.label: has confidence
entries.comment: A numeric confidence value associated with an assessment result, typically between 0 and 1.

entries.label: issued at time
entries.comment: The date-time at which an assessment result was issued or finalized.

entries.label: has phase
entries.comment: Links an enduring entity, process, or situation to one of its temporal phases.

entries.label: is phase of
entries.comment: Links a phase to the entity, process, or situation it is a temporal stage of.

entries.label: precedes
entries.comment: Asserts that one exploitation phase or event directly precedes another in the documented offense timeline. Used to build temporally ordered traversal graphs for state machine analysis of case lifecycles. The subject phase occurs before the object phase in the same investigation.

entries.label: assesses
entries.comment: Links an assessment result to the entity it evaluates.

entries.label: generated by
entries.comment: Links an assessment result to the event, action, tool, or process that produced it.

entries.label: uses method
entries.comment: Links an assessment result or event to the method, algorithm, or technique used.

entries.label: AI-Generated CSAM
entries.comment: Child sexual abuse material fully generated by artificial intelligence without depicting real victims, but still contributing to objectification and sexualization of children. Enhanced as gUFO Object for precise foundational modeling.

entries.label: AI-Altered CSAM
entries.comment: Existing CSAM that has been modified using AI techniques to alter appearance, age, or other characteristics. Enhanced as gUFO Object with alteration tracking.

entries.label: Deepfake CSAM
entries.comment: CSAM created by using AI to alter genuine content, potentially making real victims appear in fabricated scenarios or altering existing abuse material. Enhanced as gUFO Object with manipulation tracking.

entries.label: Synthetic Media CSAM
entries.comment: Completely synthetic media generated using AI models trained on large datasets, creating realistic but artificial depictions. Enhanced as gUFO Object for synthetic media modeling.

entries.label: Hybrid CSAM
entries.comment: Content combining real and AI-generated elements, making it difficult to distinguish between authentic and artificial material. Enhanced as gUFO Object with composition modeling.

entries.label: Nudified CSAM
entries.comment: Child sexual abuse material created by AI-enabled nudification (synthetic nudity) of an existing image or video. This models 'nudifying functionalities' discussed in policy contexts.

entries.label: AI Content Generation
entries.comment: Process of creating artificial CSAM using machine learning models, neural networks, or other AI technologies. Enhanced as gUFO Event for precise temporal and causal modeling.

entries.label: Model Training
entries.comment: Process of training AI models on datasets that may include illegal content for the purpose of generating new CSAM. Enhanced as gUFO Event with training phases.

entries.label: Image Generation
entries.comment: Generation of static images using AI models such as diffusion models, GANs, or other generative techniques. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Video Generation
entries.comment: Generation of video content using AI models capable of creating temporal sequences and motion. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Face Swapping
entries.comment: AI technique for replacing faces in existing content with different faces, potentially placing victims in abusive scenarios. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Age Progression
entries.comment: AI technique for artificially aging or de-aging subjects in content, potentially creating illegal material from legal content. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Nudification
entries.comment: AI content generation/manipulation process that produces synthetic nudity (e.g., 'nudifying apps' / nudifying functionalities) from existing media. Modeled as a gUFO Event and UCO Action.

entries.label: AI Content Detection
entries.comment: Process of identifying AI-generated or AI-altered content to distinguish from authentic material during investigations. Enhanced as gUFO Event for forensic process modeling.

entries.label: Synthetic Media Analysis
entries.comment: Forensic analysis of media to determine if it was artificially generated and identify generation techniques used. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Deepfake Detection
entries.comment: Specialized analysis for detecting deepfake technology use in content, including face replacement and manipulation. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Artifact Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of digital artifacts and inconsistencies that may indicate AI generation, such as compression patterns or noise characteristics. Enhanced as gUFO Event.

entries.label: has exploitation relation
entries.comment: Links enterprise to exploitation relator mediating perpetrator-victim relationships.

entries.label: historically depends on
entries.comment: Captures historical dependence between enterprise events and prior enabling events.

entries.label: participates in coercion

entries.label: participates in recruitment

entries.label: Forensic Imaging Tool
entries.comment: A tool specialized for creating forensic images of digital media using write-blocking and verification methods (e.g., FTK Imager, dd, Guymager, PALADIN).

entries.label: Mobile Forensic Tool
entries.comment: A tool specialized for mobile device forensics including logical and physical extraction (e.g., Cellebrite UFED, MSAB XRY, Oxygen Detective Suite).

entries.label: Network Forensic Tool
entries.comment: A tool specialized for network traffic analysis and packet capture (e.g., Wireshark, NetworkMiner, Xplico).

entries.label: Memory Forensic Tool
entries.comment: A tool specialized for analyzing volatile memory dumps (e.g., Volatility, Rekall, MAGNET RAM Capture).

entries.label: Hashing Tool
entries.comment: A tool specialized for generating cryptographic hashes for evidence verification (e.g., hashdeep, md5deep, NIST NSRL).

entries.label: Forensic Acquisition Action
entries.comment: The action of creating a forensically sound copy of digital evidence using write-blocking and verification procedures.

entries.label: Chain of Custody Action
entries.comment: An action that documents evidence handling, transfer, and custody maintaining legal admissibility.

entries.label: Evidence Verification Action
entries.comment: The action of verifying evidence integrity using cryptographic hashes and comparison methods.

entries.label: Timeline Analysis Action
entries.comment: The action of creating chronological sequences of digital artifacts and events for investigation analysis.

entries.label: Metadata Extraction Action
entries.comment: The action of extracting metadata from digital artifacts including EXIF, file system timestamps, and application metadata.

entries.label: Victim Identification Process
entries.comment: Systematic process for identifying child victims from seized images and videos during long-term investigations.

entries.label: Image Analysis for Victim Identification
entries.comment: Analysis of seized images to identify and remove child victims from continued exploitation.

entries.label: Cross Reference Analysis
entries.comment: Cross-referencing of digital evidence across multiple cases and international databases for victim identification.

entries.label: Victim Removal Action
entries.comment: Action taken to remove identified victims from further harm and exploitation.

entries.label: Extended Investigation Timeline
entries.comment: Investigation timeline spanning weeks, months, or years for complex child exploitation cases.

entries.label: Acquisition Phase
entries.comment: Phase involving forensic acquisition of digital evidence.

entries.label: Analysis Phase
entries.comment: Phase involving detailed forensic analysis of acquired evidence.

entries.label: Reporting Phase
entries.comment: Phase involving preparation of forensic reports and findings.

entries.label: Testimony Phase
entries.comment: Phase involving expert testimony and courtroom presentation.

entries.label: Forensic Image
entries.comment: A bit-for-bit copy of digital media created using forensically sound methods, maintaining evidence integrity.

entries.label: Recovered File
entries.comment: A file recovered from deleted or unallocated space on digital media through forensic analysis techniques.

entries.label: Memory Dump
entries.comment: A snapshot of volatile system memory captured for forensic analysis.

entries.label: Network Capture
entries.comment: A capture of network traffic packets for forensic analysis.

entries.label: Custody Document
entries.comment: Documentation recording the handling and transfer of evidence maintaining chain of custody.

entries.label: Forensic Examiner Role
entries.comment: Role of a person conducting digital forensic examination and analysis.

entries.label: Evidence Custodian Role
entries.comment: Role of a person responsible for evidence custody and security.

entries.label: Victim Identification Specialist
entries.comment: Role of specialist focused on identifying child victims from digital evidence.

entries.label: K9 Assisted Forensics
entries.comment: Forensic process enhanced by K9 detection capabilities for electronic storage devices.

entries.label: Electronic Storage Device Detection
entries.comment: Specialized detection of electronic storage devices using K9 or advanced scanning methods.

entries.label: Hidden Device Recovery
entries.comment: Recovery of concealed or hidden electronic storage devices during search operations.

entries.label: Advanced Search Technique
entries.comment: Specialized search techniques for locating digital evidence.

entries.label: Detection Dog Assist
entries.comment: Assistance provided by trained detection dogs in forensic searches.

entries.label: Mass Digital Evidence Processing
entries.comment: Processing of massive volumes of digital evidence requiring specialized automated tools and distributed processing systems (terabytes of data from platforms with millions of users).

entries.label: Automated Content Analysis
entries.comment: Automated analysis of large volumes of content using machine learning and AI for rapid classification and triage.

entries.label: Distributed Forensic Processing
entries.comment: Forensic processing distributed across multiple systems and locations for handling massive evidence volumes.

entries.label: Evidence Triage System
entries.comment: Automated system for triaging massive evidence volumes to prioritize high-value targets and critical cases.

entries.label: User Behavior Forensics
entries.comment: Forensic analysis of user behavior patterns across massive user databases for investigation prioritization.

entries.label: Content Correlation Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis correlating content across multiple users and platforms for identifying networks and relationships.

entries.label: Scalable Hash Analysis
entries.comment: Hash analysis systems capable of processing millions of files against large databases of known illegal content.

entries.label: International Evidence Processing
entries.comment: Processing of evidence collected from international operations requiring coordination across multiple forensic labs.

entries.label: Cross-Platform Correlation
entries.comment: Analysis correlating evidence across multiple platforms and services to identify coordinated criminal activities.

entries.label: Geospatial Correlation
entries.comment: Correlation analysis based on geographic and location data from multiple sources.

entries.label: Temporal Pattern Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of temporal patterns and timing correlations across different pieces of evidence.

entries.label: Behavioral Fingerprinting
entries.comment: Analysis creating unique behavioral fingerprints from user activities to identify individuals across platforms.

entries.label: Communication Pattern Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of communication patterns to identify relationships and networks.

entries.label: Metadata Correlation
entries.comment: Correlation analysis of metadata across multiple files and platforms.

entries.label: Database Intelligence Integration
entries.comment: Integration and correlation against multiple international databases and intelligence sources.

entries.label: Network Traffic Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of network traffic patterns to identify suspicious communications and data transfers.

entries.label: Machine Learning Correlation
entries.comment: AI/ML-powered correlation analysis to identify complex patterns not visible through traditional methods.

entries.label: Real-Time Correlation
entries.comment: Real-time correlation analysis for immediate identification of related evidence and ongoing activities.

entries.label: Attribution Assessment
entries.comment: Analytic conclusion that two or more observables (accounts, IP addresses, devices) are controlled by the same subject, with stated confidence and method. The assessment is an interpretation layered over the correlation evidence supporting it.

entries.label: Correlation Evidence
entries.comment: Structured evidence that observables are linked by overlapping usage, records, or artifacts. Superclass for typed correlation evidence supporting attribution assessments.

entries.label: IP Correlation Evidence
entries.comment: Structured evidence of overlapping IP usage across accounts, sessions, or platforms within a date-time scope (e.g., 13 of 20 platform session IPs matching another platform's access logs for the same subscriber).

entries.label: Subscriber Record Correlation
entries.comment: Evidence linking a platform account to carrier or ISP subscriber records (e.g., produced under legal process).

entries.label: Grooming Behavior
entries.comment: Predatory behavior designed to prepare a child for abuse by building trust, isolating them, and normalizing inappropriate contact.

entries.label: Trust Building Behavior
entries.comment: Early grooming stage focused on establishing emotional connection with the child victim.

entries.label: Conditioning Behavior
entries.comment: Offender behavior that shapes victim readiness, compliance, dependency, or situational constraints preparatory to direct exploitation.

entries.label: Isolation Behavior
entries.comment: Attempts to separate child from parents, friends, or other support systems.

entries.label: Normalization Behavior
entries.comment: Gradual introduction of sexual topics to normalize inappropriate behavior.

entries.label: Enticement
entries.comment: Direct solicitation of a child to engage in illegal sexual activity or meet for such purposes.

entries.label: Sexual Exploitation
entries.comment: Direct exploitation of child for sexual purposes including solicitation of images or performances.

entries.label: Online Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming behavior conducted through online platforms and digital communication channels.

entries.label: Grooming Phase
entries.comment: A temporal phase within the grooming process.

entries.label: Initial Contact Phase
entries.comment: First phase of grooming involving initial contact and relationship establishment.

entries.label: Conditioning Phase
entries.comment: Grooming-process phase in which the offender conditions the victim or situation for exploitation — including rapport, isolation, normalization, and compliance shaping prior to the primary exploitation act.

entries.label: Trust Building Phase
entries.comment: Phase focused on building emotional connection and trust with victim.

entries.label: Isolation Phase
entries.comment: Phase aimed at separating victim from support systems and creating dependency.

entries.label: Sexualization Phase
entries.comment: Phase involving introduction of sexual content and normalization of inappropriate behavior.

entries.label: Exploitation Phase
entries.comment: Final phase involving direct sexual exploitation and abuse.

entries.label: Maintenance Phase
entries.comment: Ongoing phase to maintain control and continue exploitation.

entries.label: Grooming Message
entries.comment: Communication containing grooming behavior or inappropriate content directed at a child.

entries.label: Sexual Solicitation
entries.comment: Message explicitly requesting sexual activity, images, or meetings from a child.

entries.label: Inappropriate Gift
entries.comment: Offer or provision of gifts, money, or favors as part of grooming process.

entries.label: Secrecy Request
entries.comment: Instruction to keep communication or relationship secret from parents or authorities.

entries.label: Victim Response
entries.comment: Child's response to grooming behavior, indicating compliance, resistance, or confusion.

entries.label: Grooming Pattern
entries.comment: Identifiable pattern of behavior across multiple communications or interactions that indicates grooming.

entries.label: Escalation Pattern
entries.comment: Progressive increase in inappropriate content or requests over time.

entries.label: Manipulation Pattern
entries.comment: Systematic use of psychological manipulation techniques to control victim.

entries.label: Prey Behavior Pattern
entries.comment: Pattern of targeting vulnerable children or specific victim characteristics.

entries.label: Online Grooming Situation
entries.comment: Overall situation encompassing the grooming relationship and interactions.

entries.label: Victim Vulnerability Situation
entries.comment: Circumstances that make a child more susceptible to grooming.

entries.label: Online Predation Situation
entries.comment: Active situation where predator is engaging with potential victims.

entries.label: Child Victim
entries.comment: Minor child who is the target of grooming behavior. When analysis depends on the victim’s exact age at specific grooming events (e.g., 13-or-younger online grooming in 2025), that age SHOULD be represented using one or more cacontology-temporal:AgeAtTimeSituation instances linked to the underlying person.

entries.label: Online Predator
entries.comment: Individual who engages in grooming behavior toward children online. Age-at-time for this offender MAY be captured via cacontology-temporal:AgeAtTimeSituation instances when age-gap and legal-capacity reasoning is required.

entries.label: Victim Vulnerability
entries.comment: Characteristics or circumstances that make a child more susceptible to grooming.

entries.label: Trust Building
entries.comment: Trust-rapport conditioning behavior establishing emotional connection with the child victim.

entries.label: Isolation Tactics
entries.comment: Isolation conditioning behavior separating the victim from support systems.

entries.label: Anonymous Platform Contact
entries.comment: Initial contact made through platforms that allow anonymous messaging or minimal user verification.

entries.label: Unverified User Profile
entries.comment: User account with minimal or no identity verification enabling anonymous contact.

entries.label: Anonymous Initiation
entries.comment: Starting contact without revealing true identity or personal information.

entries.label: Platform Anonymity Feature
entries.comment: Platform features that enable anonymous communication (guest messaging, temporary accounts, no profile requirements).

entries.label: Trust Through Anonymity
entries.comment: Building trust by appearing less threatening through anonymous contact.

entries.label: Online to Offline Progression
entries.comment: Escalation from online grooming to arranging physical meetings or contact.

entries.label: Physical Meeting Arrangement
entries.comment: Coordination of in-person meeting between predator and victim.

entries.label: Travel Arrangement
entries.comment: Planning or facilitating travel for victim to meet predator.

entries.label: Interstate Transport Plan
entries.comment: Planning to transport victim across state lines for illegal purposes.

entries.label: Victim Compliance in Physical Meeting
entries.comment: Victim's agreement or compliance with arranged physical meeting.

entries.label: Location Specific Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that references or prepares for specific physical locations.

entries.label: Offline Control Establishment
entries.comment: Establishing control over victim in preparation for physical contact.

entries.label: Educator Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming behavior by educational personnel leveraging position of trust and authority.

entries.label: Position of Trust Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that exploits educator's position of trust and authority over students.

entries.label: Peer Persona Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming using false peer identity to establish rapport with victims.

entries.label: Teenage Impersonation Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming involving impersonation of teenage peer to gain victim trust.

entries.label: Multiple Account Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming using multiple fake accounts to maintain deceptive identity.

entries.label: Cross Institutional Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming targeting students from multiple educational institutions.

entries.label: Fabricated Persona
entries.comment: A fabricated identity (e.g., a fictitious minor peer) created and controlled by an offender to contact, groom, lure, or coerce victims. The same persona may be reused across victims and platforms. Complements PeerPersonaGrooming / TeenageImpersonationGrooming behavior classes: the behavior classes type the grooming activity, while FabricatedPersona types the persona artifact itself. See also…

entries.label: Sexual Content Exchange Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming involving exchange of sexual content to normalize sexual behavior.

entries.label: Initiator Content Sending
entries.comment: Grooming phase where perpetrator sends sexual content to victim first.

entries.label: Reciprocity Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming technique encouraging victim to reciprocate with sexual content.

entries.label: Normalization Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming technique to normalize sexual conversations and content sharing.

entries.label: Graphic Conversation Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming involving progressively graphic sexual conversations.

entries.label: Victim Targeting
entries.comment: The process by which an offender identifies and selects a potential victim.

entries.label: Elite Institution Targeting
entries.comment: Targeting of students from elite or prestigious educational institutions.

entries.label: Privileged Victim Targeting
entries.comment: Targeting of victims from privileged backgrounds who may be less likely to report.

entries.label: Reputation Based Silencing
entries.comment: Exploitation of institutional reputation to discourage victim reporting.

entries.label: Rapid Escalation Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming with accelerated timeline from initial contact to exploitation attempt, bypassing traditional relationship-building phases.

entries.label: Same Day Progression
entries.comment: Grooming progression from initial contact to sexual exploitation within the same day.

entries.label: Immediate Exploitation Attempt
entries.comment: Attempt to immediately exploit victim without extended grooming or relationship building.

entries.label: Skipped Grooming Phases
entries.comment: Grooming that bypasses traditional conditioning phases such as trust building, isolation, and normalization.

entries.label: Opportunistic Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that exploits immediate opportunities rather than planned relationship development.

entries.label: Accelerated Trust Exploitation
entries.comment: Rapid exploitation of minimal trust established through pretexts or assistance offers.

entries.label: Direct Trafficking Proposition Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming involving explicit, immediate propositions for commercial sexual activity without gradual normalization.

entries.label: Explicit Commercial Offer Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming involving direct offers of money in exchange for sexual services.

entries.label: Economic Incentive Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that emphasizes financial benefits of commercial sexual activity.

entries.label: Blunt Recruitment Grooming
entries.comment: Direct, unsubtle recruitment for trafficking without gradual persuasion techniques.

entries.label: Immediate Monetization Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming focused on immediate monetization of victim's sexuality.

entries.label: Substance Facilitated Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that uses alcohol or drugs to reduce victim resistance and facilitate exploitation.

entries.label: Impairment Based Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that exploits victim impairment from substances to reduce resistance.

entries.label: Substance Induced Vulnerability Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that creates vulnerability through substance administration.

entries.label: Alcohol Facilitated Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming using alcohol to impair victim judgment and reduce resistance.

entries.label: Marijuana Facilitated Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming using marijuana to reduce victim inhibitions and facilitate exploitation.

entries.label: Physical Space Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that occurs in physical spaces rather than digital platforms.

entries.label: Street Based Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that begins with street-based contact and recruitment.

entries.label: Vehicle Based Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that uses vehicles for isolation and exploitation.

entries.label: Isolation Based Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that relies on physical isolation to reduce victim resistance.

entries.label: Public to Private Grooming
entries.comment: Grooming that transitions from public contact to private exploitation.

entries.label: Sexual Consequence Game Grooming
entries.comment: Physical-space grooming pattern where the perpetrator frames sexualized contact as part of a game with consequences, typically involving multiple juveniles in a group context (e.g., sleepovers, peer gatherings, family events).

entries.label: Account Replacement Event
entries.comment: Pattern where an offender whose account is banned or blocked creates a new account and returns to an earlier offense phase (typically initial contact). The lifecycle resets rather than terminates — structurally distinct from a coercion cycle.

entries.label: has grooming phase begin point
entries.comment: Temporal begin point for grooming phase.

entries.label: has grooming phase end point
entries.comment: Temporal end point for grooming phase.

entries.label: has role begin point
entries.comment: Temporal begin point for grooming role.

entries.label: has role end point
entries.comment: Temporal end point for grooming role.

entries.label: grooming phase duration
entries.comment: Duration of grooming phase.

entries.label: grooming stage
entries.comment: Behavior-axis stage tag on GroomingBehavior instances (not the offense-trajectory phase class used in state machines).

entries.label: conditioning mode
entries.comment: Dominant conditioning mechanism on a grooming ConditioningPhase instance or ConditioningBehavior instance.

entries.label: trust building method
entries.comment: Method used to build trust during conditioning (active_listening, emotional_support, shared_interests, etc.).

entries.label: trust level
entries.comment: Assessed level of trust established during trust-rapport conditioning.

entries.label: trust development rate
entries.comment: Rate at which trust is developed during conditioning, typically between 0.0 and 1.0.

entries.label: behavior duration
entries.comment: Length of time grooming behavior continued (in days).

entries.label: communication frequency
entries.comment: Frequency of contact with victim (daily, weekly, multiple_daily).

entries.label: content type
entries.comment: Type of content in grooming message (text, image, video, audio).

entries.label: explicitness level

entries.label: Module Integration Strategy

entries.label: Medium Priority Module

entries.label: Low Priority Module

entries.label: Platform Infrastructure
entries.comment: Technical infrastructure supporting child exploitation platforms, including servers, networks, and supporting systems (gUFO Object).

entries.label: Server Infrastructure
entries.comment: Server and hosting infrastructure supporting platform operations, including web servers, database servers, and application servers (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Content Delivery Network
entries.comment: CDN infrastructure used for distributing illegal content globally with high availability and performance (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Database Infrastructure
entries.comment: Database systems storing user accounts, content metadata, and platform operational data (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Network Infrastructure
entries.comment: Network topology and routing infrastructure supporting platform connectivity and distribution (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Payment Processing
entries.comment: Financial processing systems enabling platform monetization through subscription fees, content purchases, or cryptocurrency transactions (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Cryptocurrency Infrastructure
entries.comment: Cryptocurrency wallets, exchanges, and payment processing systems used for anonymous financial transactions (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Subscription Management
entries.comment: Systems managing user subscriptions, access levels, and recurring payment processing (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Financial Obfuscation
entries.comment: Methods used to obscure financial transactions and payment flows to avoid detection (gUFO Object).

entries.label: Hosting Provider
entries.comment: Organizations providing server hosting, cloud services, or infrastructure-as-a-service for platforms (gUFO Object).

entries.label: Domain Infrastructure
entries.comment: Domain name system infrastructure including domain registration, DNS services, and subdomain management (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Proxy Infrastructure
entries.comment: Proxy servers and reverse proxy systems used to hide platform origins and provide redundancy (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Load Balancer
entries.comment: Load balancing infrastructure distributing traffic across multiple servers for high availability (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Security Infrastructure
entries.comment: Security systems protecting platform infrastructure from detection and takedown efforts (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Encryption Infrastructure
entries.comment: Encryption systems protecting data transmission, storage, and user communications (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Anonymity Infrastructure
entries.comment: Systems providing anonymity to users and operators, including Tor integration and VPN services (gUFO FunctionalComplex).

entries.label: Geographic Distribution
entries.comment: Geographic distribution of infrastructure across multiple countries to complicate law enforcement efforts (gUFO Object).

entries.label: Infrastructure Takedown
entries.comment: Coordinated operation to dismantle platform infrastructure including servers, domains, and supporting systems (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Server Seizure
entries.comment: Physical or virtual seizure of servers hosting platform infrastructure (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Domain Sinkholing
entries.comment: Redirecting domain traffic to law enforcement controlled servers to gather intelligence (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Account Freezing
entries.comment: Freezing financial accounts and cryptocurrency wallets associated with platform operations (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Data Mirror Creation
entries.comment: Creating forensic mirrors of seized infrastructure for analysis and evidence preservation (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Infrastructure Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of seized infrastructure to understand platform operations and identify additional targets (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Network Topology Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of network architecture and connectivity patterns within platform infrastructure (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Financial Flow Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of financial transactions and payment flows through platform monetization systems (gUFO Event).

entries.label: User Access Pattern Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of user access patterns and geographic distribution based on infrastructure logs (gUFO Event).

entries.label: Social Media Platform
entries.comment: A digital platform for social networking and content sharing (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Twitter, LinkedIn). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Messaging Service
entries.comment: A digital service for real-time communication and messaging (e.g., WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Discord, Kik). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Video Streaming Platform
entries.comment: A platform for video content streaming and sharing (e.g., YouTube, Twitch, OnlyFans, Periscope). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: File Hosting Service
entries.comment: A service for storing and sharing files online (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, MEGA). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Game Platform
entries.comment: A digital platform for gaming with communication features (e.g., Xbox Live, PlayStation Network, Steam, Roblox, Minecraft). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Dark Web Service
entries.comment: A service accessible through anonymizing networks like Tor, often used for illegal activities. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Online Dating Platform
entries.comment: A platform for meeting and dating online (e.g., Tinder, Bumble, Grindr, dating websites). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Cryptocurrency Service
entries.comment: A service for cryptocurrency transactions and exchanges (e.g., Bitcoin, Coinbase, Binance). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Electronic Service Provider (ESP)
entries.comment: An organization that provides digital services and platforms, with responsibilities for content moderation and law enforcement cooperation. Modeled as gUFO Organization.

entries.label: Technical Service Provider
entries.comment: Organizations providing technical infrastructure (hosting, CDN, DNS, etc.) that may be involved in content distribution. Modeled as gUFO Organization.

entries.label: Content Moderation Capability
entries.comment: The ability and methods a platform uses to detect, review, and remove inappropriate content. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Content Moderation Queue
entries.comment: A queue/backlog of content items awaiting moderation review and operational handling at scale (e.g., large volumes of flagged CSAM candidates).

entries.label: Review Backlog Situation
entries.comment: Situation in which moderation review demand exceeds capacity, producing review backlog/latency risks.

entries.label: Moderation Throughput Metrics
entries.comment: Operational metrics describing moderation throughput and latency (e.g., queue size, review latency, flagged volume).

entries.label: Data Retention Policy
entries.comment: A platform's policy for how long they retain user data and content. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Legal Compliance Capability
entries.comment: A platform's ability to respond to legal requests and cooperate with law enforcement. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: User Verification System
entries.comment: Systems used by platforms to verify user identity and age. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Content Moderation Action
entries.comment: An action taken by a platform to moderate content (review, remove, restrict, etc.). Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Account Suspension Action
entries.comment: An action to suspend or terminate a user account due to policy violations. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Data Preservation Action
entries.comment: An action to preserve user data in response to legal requests. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Legal Data Disclosure Action
entries.comment: An action to disclose user data to law enforcement in response to legal process. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Emergency Disclosure Request
entries.comment: Time-sensitive request by law enforcement/investigators to an electronic service provider for immediate disclosure of information based on an asserted emergency involving imminent danger (e.g., danger of death or serious physical injury). Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Content Hashing Action
entries.comment: An action by a platform to generate hashes of content for detection and matching. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Large Scale Platform Takedown
entries.comment: Coordinated takedown of major exploitation platforms with user bases exceeding 1 million accounts, requiring specialized international coordination and mass forensic processing. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Platform Operation
entries.comment: Coordinated law enforcement operation targeting specific platforms or services. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Mass User Behavior Analysis
entries.comment: Analysis of user behavior patterns across massive user bases for investigation prioritization and automated threat assessment. Modeled as gUFO Event.

entries.label: Mass User Database
entries.comment: User database analysis for platforms with massive user bases requiring specialized processing techniques and automated analysis tools. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: User Scale Classification
entries.comment: Classification system for platform size based on user base: small (<1K), medium (1K-100K), large (100K-1M), massive (1M+). Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: User Risk Classification
entries.comment: Automated classification of user risk levels based on platform activity patterns, content sharing, and behavioral indicators. Modeled as gUFO Object.

entries.label: Platform Deployment Phase
entries.comment: Phase when platform is deployed and becomes operational. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Phase.

entries.label: Platform Growth Phase
entries.comment: Phase of platform expansion and user base growth. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Phase.

entries.label: Platform Moderation Phase
entries.comment: Phase of active content moderation and policy enforcement. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Phase.

entries.label: Platform Investigation Phase
entries.comment: Phase when platform is under law enforcement investigation. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Phase.

entries.label: Platform Takedown Phase
entries.comment: Phase of platform takedown and shutdown operations. Modeled as anti-rigid gUFO Phase.

entries.label: Massive Platform Situation
entries.comment: Situation involving platforms with massive user bases requiring specialized investigation approaches. Modeled as gUFO Situation.

entries.label: Multi-Platform Situation
entries.comment: Situation involving coordination across multiple platforms and service providers. Modeled as gUFO Situation.

entries.label: Platform Cooperation Situation
entries.comment: Situation involving cooperative efforts between platforms and law enforcement. Modeled as gUFO Situation.

entries.label: Social Media Evidence
entries.comment: Digital evidence collected from social media platforms, including posts, messages, and account information.

entries.label: Social Media Account
entries.comment: User account on a social media platform potentially containing evidence.

entries.label: Cross-Platform Evidence
entries.comment: Evidence found across multiple social media platforms by the same user.

entries.label: Social Media Post
entries.comment: Individual posts, updates, or content shared on social media platforms.

entries.label: Private Message
entries.comment: Private messages or direct communications on social media platforms.

entries.label: Account Metadata
entries.comment: Account-level metadata including creation date, profile information, and activity patterns.

entries.label: Electronic Device Evidence
entries.comment: Digital evidence found on electronic devices including computers, phones, and storage media.

entries.label: Device Social Media Correlation
entries.comment: Correlation between evidence found on devices and social media accounts.

entries.label: Stored Social Media Content
entries.comment: Social media content downloaded and stored on electronic devices.

entries.label: Social Media App Data
entries.comment: Application data from social media apps stored on devices.

entries.label: Platform Investigation Coordination
entries.comment: Coordinated investigation across multiple platforms and devices.

entries.label: Simultaneous Search Warrant
entries.comment: Coordinated search warrant execution on devices and platform accounts.

entries.label: Digital Evidence Correlation
entries.comment: Process of correlating evidence found across devices and platforms.

entries.label: Anonymous Chat Platform
entries.comment: Platform that allows anonymous or minimally verified communication, enabling contact without identity verification.

entries.label: Guest Chat Feature
entries.comment: Platform feature allowing users to chat without creating accounts or verifying identity.

entries.label: Temporary Account System
entries.comment: System allowing creation of temporary accounts with minimal verification requirements.

entries.label: Minimal Verification Requirement
entries.comment: Verification requirements that are easily bypassed or minimal (email only, no identity check).

entries.label: Anonymous Contact Opportunity
entries.comment: Opportunities provided by platform for anonymous users to initiate contact with other users.

entries.label: Random User Matching
entries.comment: Platform feature that randomly matches users for anonymous conversations.

entries.label: Open Chat Rooms
entries.comment: Chat rooms open to anonymous users without verification or moderation.

entries.label: Profile Browsing Anonymous
entries.comment: Ability to browse and contact user profiles anonymously without revealing identity.

entries.label: Anonymity Protection Level
entries.comment: Level of anonymity protection provided by platform features and policies.

entries.label: Identity Disclosure Policy
entries.comment: Platform policy regarding when and how user identities may be disclosed to other users or authorities.

entries.label: Platform Affordance
entries.comment: A platform capability that offenders may misuse to advance an offense trajectory (anonymity, ephemerality, unmonitored communication, etc.).

entries.label: Anonymity Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance enabling pseudonymous or minimally verified contact.

entries.label: Ephemerality Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance where messages or media auto-delete, reducing forensic retention on the platform.

entries.label: Unmonitored Communication Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance for private channels with limited proactive moderation or parental visibility.

entries.label: Contact Discovery Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance for finding or matching with new contacts (search, suggestions, random matching).

entries.label: Distribution Infrastructure Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance for sharing or broadcasting content to audiences beyond direct dyadic chat.

entries.label: Generative Synthesis Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance for AI-generated or synthetic media creation and manipulation.

entries.label: Coordination Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance for group coordination, encrypted channels, or multi-party planning.

entries.label: Coercion Leverage Affordance
entries.comment: Platform affordance that amplifies coercive leverage (screenshots, forwarding, contact export, payment rails).

entries.label: Channel Migration Event
entries.comment: Documented offense pattern where contact is initiated on one platform and deliberately moved to a second platform before escalation, to access more capable channels and/or sever the evidence trail on the originating platform.

entries.label: Affordance Misuse
entries.comment: Annotation linking a platform affordance to the phase transition it enabled — affordances on offense trajectory edges rather than platform nodes alone.
